articles.title: The dynasties, elites, and parties competing for power in BARMM
articles.summary: Thirteen regional political parties and nearly 700 candidates from dynasties and those with ties to the MILF and MNLF are vying for power in the Bangsomoro Parliament

blocks.text: Decades of conflict and peacebuilding will culminate on Monday, September 14 — the day when more than two million Filipinos of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) will cast their votes in the regional parliamentary elections.

The momentous elections matter not just because it is the first of its kind but because the Bangsamoro people will decide the set of leaders that will hopefully overcome the region’s challenges of self-governance and its history of neglect and underdevelopment.

The people’s memory of the Moro struggle, infused with the trauma of rido (clan feuds), poverty, and the threat of insurgency, will be tested as the list of candidates contains aspirants belonging to the region’s powerful political dynasties and former combatants, whose loyalties lie with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and the Moro National Liberation Front or MNLF.

We’ve compiled the profiles of the candidates running in the region’s 32 districts and the 13 regional political parties all eyeing a seat in the Bangsamoro Parliament. More than just looking at family connections, the articles below also reviewed the historical rivalries and recent connections formed prior to election day.
Here are the dynasties, elites, and parties vying for power in BARMM.
There are 13 regional political parties and nearly 700 candidates seeking seats in the Bangsamoro Parliament.

While this political participation in the region may broaden and offer BARMM voters a wider range of choices, the Asian Network for Free Elections and other watchdog groups say that the heightened tensions between the parties — made worse by clan and dynastic politics — could raise concerns over peace and security during the election period.
Watch this video by Shay Du for a rundown of the political parties participating in the historic polls.

blocks.caption: The dynasties, elites, and parties competing for power in BARMM

blocks.text: Over two dozen members of political dynasties, Islamic scholars, lawmakers, and youth leaders are competing for Lanao del Sur’s seats in the Bangsamoro region

The candidates have until September 12 to campaign in their respective districts. The province has 1,164 barangays and 727,634 registered voters, according to Commission on Elections data as of May 8.
Here are the electoral races in Lanao del Sur’s nine districts.

BARMM Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof “Sammy Gambar” Macacua is running in the 3rd parliamentary district of Maguindanao del Norte, where the election results could determine whether he stays or not as the region’s leader.

If Macacua wins in the September elections, he would be eligible and could be chosen by the BARMM Parliament as the first elected chief minister of the seven-year-old region. This makes the election outcome in the Maguindanao del Norte district crucial, as it could determine the direction of the region.
Here are the electoral races happening in Maguindanao del Norte’s five parliamentary districts.
Relatives of the Midtimbang, Ampatuan, Upam, and Mangudadatu clans are vying for power in Maguindanao del Sur’s five parliamentary districts.

Maguindanao del Sur is currently led by Governor Ali Musa Midtimbang, whose family formed an alliance with the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) during the 2025 local election. Ali’s nephew, Member of Parliament Tawakal Midtimbang, is running in the 1st District.

The elder Midtimbang’s seat was previously held by Mariam Sangki Mangudadatu, the last governor of the once-undivided Maguindanao, whose relative is now vying for a seat in the Bangsamoro Parliament through Maguindanao del Sur’s 4th District.
Here are the electoral races happening in Maguindanao del Sur.

The Hatamans are seeking a larger foothold in Basilan’s delegation to the BARMM Parliament, with former Basilan governor and now Vice Governor Hadjiman “Jim” Hataman-Salliman’s son, Jimael Salam Datumanong Salliman, and nephew, Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA) Member Abrar Hataman, seeking seats in the 4th and 3rd districts, respectively.
If they win, the Hatamans would hold two of Basilan’s four parliamentary seats. Both are running under the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), now led by Macacua.
Here are the electoral races happening in the province of Basilan.

blocks.caption: People, Person, Head

blocks.text: In Tawi-Tawi’s four parliamentary districts, members of political clans, former local officials, civil society leaders, and professionals are campaigning for seats in the 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament. More than half of them have ties to local political families.

One of three Que brothers from Bongao is seeking the 1st District’s parliamentary seat. The Matba, Amilbangsa, Matolo, Jamalul, and Ahaja clans also have members in the races for the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th districts. Tawi-Tawi Governor Yshmael Sali’s sister-in-law, Rhosatina Sulayman Matolo-De Asis, is among those seeking a seat in the 3rd District.
Here are the electoral races in Tawi-Tawi’s four districts.

Cotabato City, the seat of the Bangsamoro regional government, is seeing a competitive race among seasoned public officials, educators, and other candidates, some of whom have ties to local political dynasties.

Three parliamentary seats are up for grabs in the city, whose local government until recently was led by a mayor, Mohammad Ali “Bruce” Matabalao, who supported the UBJP, the political party of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).
However, internal rifts in the MILF and the resignation of Matabalao from the UBJP have brought much speculation as to how well the MILF’s party is going to fare in Cotabato City’s 37 barangays.
Here are the electoral races in the three parliamentary districts of Cotabato City.

blocks.caption: People, Person, Adult

blocks.text: With the region’s election day fast approaching, candidates in the BARMM Special Geographic Area (SGA) are stepping up their campaigns for district parliamentary seats.

The candidates include former BARMM interim chief minister Al Haj Murad’s son Mansor and BTA Member Butch Malang in the 1st District, and several independent candidates competing against UBJP and BFP bets in the 2nd District
Here are the electoral races happening in the two parliamentary districts of the SGA.

articles.title: Trump makes highly unusual promise of $5,000 for all if Republicans win midterms | First Thing
articles.summary: Speaking in Dallas, the president raised ethical concerns with an apparent $1tn offer to the electorate. Plus the US citizens who are finding moving to Scotland to be an irresistible…

blocks.text: Good morning. Donald Trump has pledged to pay every adult citizen in the US $5,000 if Republicans retain the House and Senate in the midterm elections. The outlandish proposal, which would cost over $1tn, immediately raised ethical concerns.

Trump made the promise during a marathon speech at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas in which he assailed Democrats as “radical”, defended his unpopular war in Iran, and urged voters to “pretend that I’m on the ballot”. Trump claimed, without evidence, that his second term had been “the most successful two years, financially and every other way, in the history of the presidency”.

In a statement, Ken Martin, the chair of the Democratic National Committee, accused Republicans of holding a “bizarre dog-and-pony show” to placate the president’s “fragile ego”. “Tonight only confirmed that the president is a lame duck failure who is dragging his party toward defeat,” Martin said.

items: Why did the Republicans hold a midterm convention? Republicans are gambling that the GOP’s first midterm convention can salvage their threatened House majority. However, Donald Trump’s dismal approval rating drove many competitive candidates to skip the two-day event entirely.

What has Trump said about the former attorney Michael Cohen? The US president has said he would consider pardoning Michael Cohen, the former fixer whom he once branded a “rat” for testifying against him. Cohen was Trump’s personal lawyer, but flipped in 2018, and pleaded guilty to federal crimes including facilitating a hush payment to the pornography star Stormy Daniels and lying under oath to Congress.

blocks.text: Rubio says US will work with allies to stop drug-trafficking as three killed in latest boat strike

blocks.caption: Marco Rubio speaks to the press outside the US embassy in Quito. Photograph: Dolores Ochoa/AP

blocks.text: The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said the Trump administration was focused on working with allied countries and aligning with their laws but insisted the military will “still blow up ships if need be”. The statement comes a year after Washington began a campaign of unilateral deadly strikes against those it calls “narco-terrorists” operating boats in international waters.

“I think its an incredible advance for the first time to have countries that are willing to participate in these efforts in their territorial waters,” Rubio told reporters on a trip to the Ecuadorian capital, Quito. “The important point is that these routes are being disrupted. These routes are being ended”.

items: How many people has the US killed in its campaign? Late Wednesday, US Southern Command announced the latest strike in the Caribbean Sea, saying it killed three people. That brought the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the US military to at least 230 in 69 strikes.

What has the US announced about Ecuador’s gangs? The US has designated Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones gang as a terrorist organisation. Rubio said the gang was linked to narcotics trafficking, as well as attacks on civilians, law enforcement officers and journalists. “We are talking about terrorists who, in many cases, possess weapons and equipment resembling the national armies of certain countries,” he said.

blocks.text: Apple unveils folding iPhone Duo … and its new CEO

blocks.caption: Apple CEO John Ternus, alongside vice-president of industrial design Molly Anderson, showing off the new iPhone Duo. Photograph: Karl Mondon/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Apple has unveiled the iPhone Duo, the company’s first foldable phone and the most significant change to the iPhone since its 2007 introduction. The nearly $2,000 device takes inspiration from iPads’ wide screens, and when opened, is the company’s largest phone display and thinnest phone.

While competitors have been releasing foldable smartphones since the late 2010s, the new model is a first for Apple, and its rollout serves as the first big test for its new CEO, John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook last week. The phone will be available on 23 October.

items: What did new CEO Ternus say about his role? Helming the company’s annual showcase for the first time, Ternus said: “I want to take a moment to express what an extraordinary privilege it is to represent the remarkable teams here at Apple. I continue to be inspired every single day by the curiosity, invention and relentless pursuit of excellence that define Apple.”

blocks.text: Anthropic researchers say AI could cause human extinction by 2030

blocks.caption: Anthropic has been accused of ignoring the extent of the threat from artificial intelligence. Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters

blocks.text: Artificial intelligence could kill off humanity within the decade, according to three researchers with the industry giant Anthropic, one of whom has quit his job in protest. Jacob Coxon accused Anthropic and his previous employer, OpenAI, of ignoring or, at best, mishandling their response to the threat.

He said “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt. No other human activity poses this level of danger.” Lawmakers including Ted Cruz and Bernie Sanders have raised concerns following Coxon’s words.

articles.title: More troops, tanks coming to beef up security for Bangsamoro polls
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur — The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is set to deploy armored personnel carriers (APCs), mobile artillery systems, additional ground troops and air…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur — The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is set to deploy armored personnel carriers (APCs), mobile artillery systems, additional ground troops and air assets to Lanao del Sur as part of intensified security measures for the Bangsamoro Parliamentary Elections (BPE) on Sept. 14.

Maj. Noelio Brigole, spokesperson of the Army’s 1st Infantry (Tabak) Division, said the additional deployment forms part of the AFP’s regular election security measures, which include the strategic positioning and movement of troops and assets to areas requiring additional support.

The augmentation includes Sabrah tanks and ATMOS (Autonomous Truck Mounted Howitzer System) 155mm artillery systems, which will reinforce armored and fire-support units already prepositioned in the province, complementing the 10 battalions currently deployed there.

The 29th and 30th Infantry Battalions will also serve as follow-on forces, while Black Hawk and T129 ATAK helicopters will provide aviation support to enhance mobility, surveillance, and responsiveness throughout the election period.

“These preparations are preventive and protective in nature,” Brigole said, stressing that the strengthened posture is designed to deter lawless armed elements from resorting to violence or intimidation.
Brigole did not say when the additional augmentation will be deployed.
He noted that the AFP’s presence should not cause alarm among local communities but instead encourage voters to freely exercise their democratic rights.
The Tabak Division assured residents that the coordinated deployment of troops and assets reflects the AFP’s continuing commitment to peace and stability.
“Our mission is to help ensure the safe, peaceful, and orderly conduct of the elections,” Brigole said. /mr

articles.title: Cebu builds PPP pipeline as province seeks investments, jobs
articles.summary: Cebu is preparing infrastructure and development projects for possible private investment as the province seeks to bring in more businesses and jobs. ... Keep on reading: Cebu builds PPP pipeline as…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Cebu is preparing infrastructure and development projects for possible private investment as the province seeks to bring in more businesses and jobs.
According to the Provincial Information Office, the initiative is part of the provincial government’s effort to address development needs while making Cebu more attractive to investors.

On September 9, the provincial government formalized its partnership with the national government’s Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Center to help turn potential projects into investment-ready proposals.
Building the PPP pipeline
Gov. Pamela Baricuatro and PPP Center Deputy Executive Director Eleazar Ricote signed the memorandum of agreement during the second day of the Cebu Economic Forum 4.0.
Through the partnership, the province can work with the PPP Center in determining which infrastructure projects are suitable for private-sector involvement.
The center will assist in reviewing proposed projects, studying their feasibility, and developing the requirements needed to move them through government approval and procurement.

It will also help the province identify projects that could receive assistance through the Project Development and Monitoring Facility, including funding for feasibility studies and transaction advisory services.
The PPP Center is the national government agency that assists public agencies in developing projects that may be carried out through public-private partnerships.
Wider opportunities
The agreement also opens the possibility of projects involving several local government units or areas across Cebu and Central Visayas.
These may cover connectivity, shared services, investment promotion, and other projects intended to support economic development in the region.
The province will form its own PPP team and assign a permanent focal person to oversee the projects and coordinate with the PPP Center.

“The purpose of this MOA is to provide a framework for cooperation and coordination between the Parties with the goal of developing a robust pipeline of PPP projects for the Province of Cebu,” the agreement states.
The partnership provides the province with a process for assessing projects before they are offered for possible private-sector participation.
Investment push
The partnership followed the provincial government’s presentation of investment opportunities during the forum’s opening day on September 8.
The two-day forum featured possible investments involving cities and municipalities, provincial government assets, PPP projects, and financing options available to businesses.

“To our investors and business community: Come to Cebu. Invest in Cebu. Grow with Cebu. We welcome investments that create jobs, introduce new technologies, strengthen our industries, and prepare us for the future,” Baricuatro said, as shared by the Provincial Information Office.

She also cited efforts to make it easier for businesses to operate in the province by simplifying procedures, shortening transaction times, clarifying requirements, and improving government responsiveness.
The forum drew potential investors from China, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, India, Thailand, Singapore, the United States, Canada, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Ukraine.

The Cebu Economic Forum 4.0 was held on September 8 and 9 at the Capitol Social Hall, where government and business representatives discussed investment prospects, financing, and development opportunities in Cebu.

articles.title: RNLI steps up security after attacks by far-right agitators over small boat rescues
articles.summary: Volunteers told to consider not wearing branded clothing and to shut lifeboat stations if they feel in danger

blocks.text: The RNLI is stepping up security after a backlash from far-right agitators over the lifeboat charity’s involvement in rescuing asylum seekers in the Channel and landing them on UK shores.
Volunteers have been told by the charity’s bosses that they should consider not wearing RNLI branded clothing if they feel this might put them at risk.
They have also been advised that they should feel empowered to shut up shops or lifeboat stations if they feel in danger.
There has been a heavy security presence around RNLI bases on the south coast of England over the last few days with police and private guards monitoring some areas.

At the charity’s headquarters in Poole, barriers have been put in place around a memorial sculpture to RNLI volunteers who lost their lives and around a rose bed to mark the 200th anniversary of the charity. A viewing platform into the headquarters has been closed off.

The RNLI has vowed to continue to rescue asylum seekers in the Channel despite the attacks from far-right activists following its involvement in a rescue on Sunday in which a dinghy carrying asylum seekers was brought into Portsmouth.
But following Sunday’s protest, the RNLI’s chief executive emailed volunteers to say security processes were being reviewed.
As well as suggesting they consider not wearing RNLI clothing, volunteers were asked to challenge people near lifeboat stations if they did not have ID.

They were also advised not to engage with members of the public if they felt uncomfortable. Staff at the Portsmouth lifeboat station close to where the asylum seekers landed on Sunday have been approached by members of the public and asked to explain the RNLI’s actions.

The RNLI has said workers have been subjected to online and physical abuse and there have been “baseless” rumours circulating that the charity had housed asylum seekers or moved them to secret locations after helping them to shore.

Three police forces have been involved in protecting RNLI volunteers, staff and buildings. Dorset police have been helping keep the headquarters secure while Hampshire officers have patrolled RNLI stations in Portsmouth.

Sussex police are also investigating “offensive and threatening commentary towards RNLI volunteers”. Images of some RNLI crew members who were apparently involved in the operation on Sunday have been published on social media with the accusation that they were complicit in an “invasion” of the UK.
About 50 protesters including members of the Poole Patriots and Hampshire Resistance attended a demonstration outside the RNLI’s headquarters in Poole on Wednesday.
Protest leaders handed out rape alarms to women, claiming they were at risk from men brought into the UK by the RNLI, and called for people to stop donating to the charity.

articles.title: MARINA investigates Coron ship fire
articles.summary: The Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) is already looking into the fire incident on a vessel in Coron, Palawan that killed five individuals.

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 6:42pm
The Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) is already looking into the fire incident on a vessel in Coron, Palawan that killed five individuals.
MARINA said that an investigation team was already deployed and assured assistance to the 43 survivors.

"The Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) has immediately deployed an investigation team and mobilized teams from the MARINA Regional Office IV to actively coordinate with the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and provide assistance to the survivors following the fire incident involving passenger vessel MV 'June Aster' in the vicinity of Barangay Marcilla, Coron, Palawan, on 9 September 2026," the agency said.
"MARINA’s Enforcement Service (ES) has also commenced a Marine Safety Investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident," it added.
MARINA added that it will help continue to provide updates once verified information is available.
According to the Philippine Coast Guard, the fire on MV June Aster started in the cargo hold based on the initial account of one of the survivors.
The surviving crew member told authorities that the fire started small.

But authorities have yet to obtain the complete details of how the fire started, as the surviving crew member interviewed by the PCG has yet to provide a full account of the incident. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Vance appears to walk back Trump’s offer of $5,000 ‘dividend’ if Republicans win midterms – US politics live
articles.summary: Vice-president suggests payment would not go to all and would be paid for by tariff revenues despite supreme court rulings against much of Trump’s program

blocks.text: Vance appears to walk back Trump claims that US citizens will receive $5,000 if Republicans win midterms
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Vice-president JD Vance appeared to partially row back on Donald Trump’s outlandish claims that every adult citizen in the US would receive $5,000 if the Republicans retain the House and Senate in the midterm elections.

“If the Republicans win, you win with us, and you get $5,000,” Trump told a roaring crowd, during a nearly two-hour long speech at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas in which he also urged voters to “pretend that I’m on the ballot”.

But Vance, speaking after the president, suggested the so-called dividend payments would not go to the wealthy and that it could be paid for by US tariff revenues – though the suggested payment dwarfs what the US has taken in through the protectionist measures.

Congress would need to approve or otherwise acquiesce to the payment. The sum would far exceed US tariff revenues even before the Supreme Court tossed much of the president’s tariff program last year.
The White House has yet to release details on Trump’s announcement.

Surrounded by supporters waving American flag placards, Trump claimed, without evidence, that his second term had been “the most successful two years, financially and every other way, in the history of the presidency”, but devoted much of his speech to fearmongering about what would happen should Democrats win the House or the Senate for the final two years of his presidency.
“There is a crazy little sick cloud over our country,” Trump said. “We will defeat communism in America.”

The president and Republicans are gambling that throwing a midterm convention – the first the GOP has ever held – can buoy the party, which is predicted to lose control of the House. Yet, Trump’s deep unpopularity among Americans – his approval rating is hovering at about 38% – meant many Republican candidates running in competitive races skipped the two-day confab entirely.
Read the full story here:
In other developments:

items: In a nearly two-hour speech, Donald Trump capped off his first night remarks at the GOP midterm convention by pleading with Republicans to “pretend that I’m running”. The president centered himself in the battle to control Congress, and acknowledged that candidates are more successful when he is on the ballot. He offered an ominous outlook if Republicans fail to retain power.

Throughout his remarks, Trump also tried to campaign on behalf of Republicans in competitive midterm races. While he made fun of Ken Paxton’s clothing choices and the way he speaks, he praised the Republican nominee for US Senate in Texas as “the single greatest attorney general” in the state’s history, while also branding his opponent James Talarico as a “disaster”.

Earlier, Democratic senator John Fetterman made a surprise virtual appearance at the Republican midterm convention, delivering a video address supporting Dave McCormick, a Republican senator in Pennsylvania. Fetterman, who has increasingly broken with his party since his election in 2022, said in the video that he would always reject “extremes and socialism”, repeating an oft-used Republican critique of the Democratic party’s increasingly popular left wing.

Meanwhile, several Republicans who are facing tough races have chosen not to attend the convention in Dallas. This include Susan Collins, the five-term incumbent senator from Maine, and Dan Sullivan – the Republican senator from Alaska who is facing a tough contest against former Democratic congresswoman Mary Peltola.

blocks.text: Key events

items: 19m agoVance appears to walk back Trump claims that US citizens will receive $5,000 if Republicans win midterms

blocks.text: Marc Goldwein, the senior policy director at the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, a think tank in Washington, said Donald Trump has no authority send money to Americans without approval from Congress.
Goldwein added that dividends are something that companies pay when there’s a surplus, but the US is running $2tn annual deficits and has $40tn in debt.
“The idea that we’ve had fiscal success is backwards and bordering on laughable,” he said. “We don’t have surpluses to give away.”

The move was reminiscent of billionaire Elon Musk’s efforts to buy votes in last year’s Wisconsin state Supreme Court race, where he handed out million-dollar checks to voters to try to boost a candidate who ultimately lost.
Trump’s proposal would be legal because the payment would go to everyone regardless of how they voted, or whether they voted at all, said New Mexico-based attorney John Day.
“This is a campaign promise,” Day said. “It’s not a payment to individuals to try to get them to vote in a particular way.”

While he made fun of Ken Paxton’s clothing choices and the way he speaks, he praised the Republican nominee for US Senate in Texas as “the single greatest attorney general” in the state’s history, while also branding his opponent James Talarico as a “disaster”.

Earlier, Democratic senator John Fetterman made a surprise virtual appearance at the Republican midterm convention, delivering a video address supporting Dave McCormick, a Republican senator in Pennsylvania. Fetterman, who has increasingly broken with his party since his election in 2022, said in the video that he would always reject “extremes and socialism”, repeating an oft-used Republican critique of the Democratic party’s increasingly popular left wing.

Meanwhile, several Republicans who are facing tough races have chosen not to attend the convention in Dallas. This include Susan Collins, the five-term incumbent senator from Maine, and Dan Sullivan – the Republican senator from Alaska who is facing a tough contest against former Democratic congresswoman Mary Peltola.

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 6:38pm
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. wants dismissed House lawmaker Zaldy Co arrested “at all costs,” Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said Thursday.

Co, tagged as a mastermind behind the multi-billion flood control scam, has been evading Philippine authorities since 2025. Remulla is set to fly to France with the intention of bringing back the fugitive ex-lawmaker.

“That’s the agenda, that’s the agenda. Zaldy Co is the agenda … we know where he is, we know the address, we know his house. It’s to get him back here,” Remulla said in an ambush interview after the Department of the Interior and Local Government’s budget hearing at the Senate.
Remulla said that he was confident that Co could be brought back home, saying that Marcos wanted to get Co back “at all costs.”
“The truth and the law are behind us and I think we can conclusively prove that once the warrant of arrest is in order,” he said.
Asked for a target, Remulla estimated that it could take “two weeks.”
Remulla is hoping that a Red Notice will be issued by the Interpol. It is another reason why he is going to France.
Despite the lack of a Red Notice, however, Remulla said that it would still be difficult for Co to move around Europe.
Co has not sent out feelers to the government, Remulla said.

“I don't know the man. I've never met him. If I did, I don't recall, I've never had his number, we've never had contact with each other. We’ll only get in touch with him when we arrest him,” Remulla said.
Asked where his confidence is coming from, Remulla said “mayabang ako”. (I am boastful.) — RSJ GMA News

articles.title: Mandaue City nears drug-cleared status, with only 3 barangays pending
articles.summary: MANDAUE CITY, Cebu — Only three of Mandaue City’s 27 barangays need to complete the drug-clearing process, bringing the city closer to being declared a drug-cleared city. According to Niño Krisbayani…

blocks.text: MANDAUE CITY, Cebu — Only three of Mandaue City’s 27 barangays need to complete the drug-clearing process, bringing the city closer to being declared a drug-cleared city.
According to Niño Krisbayani Dargantes, officer-in-charge of the Mandaue City Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Office, 24 barangays have been declared cleared of illegal drugs.
The three remaining barangays are Jagobiao, Tipolo, and Centro.
Dargantes said that Jagobiao is already up for deliberation. Tipolo and Centro are completing the technical requirements and documents.
What Mandaue City needs to do
He said that the remaining requirements are mostly minor documents and certifications, including those needed for the validation process.

Dargantes said that the City Government is hopeful that the three remaining barangays can complete the process within the year. That supports the city government’s goal of having Mandaue City declared as drug-cleared.

The process includes house-to-house visits and verification of individuals included in the drug-clearing records. Authorities can no longer find some individuals on the drug watch list. They may have died or moved to another location different from their recorded addresses.
What does being a drug-cleared city mean?
Dargantes also clarified that being declared drug-cleared does not mean being completely freed of illegal drugs.
“I-clarify lang namo kay mao baya nay misconception sa uban,” said Dargantes. (We want to clarify that because that’s a misconception some people have.)

He said that the drug-clearing process is based on lists by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency and the Philippine National Police. Individuals on the lists undergo rehabilitation or other interventions. Officials review their cases once they complete the required interventions.
Dargantes noted that the list the agencies use dates back to 2016. This contributes to difficulties in verifying the status and whereabouts of some individuals.
Annual review for drug-cleared barangays
He urged residents and barangay officials to continue reporting suspected illegal drug activities to the PDEA and PNP. That way, these can be verified and authorities can act on them.

Meanwhile, barangays that authorities have declared drug-cleared continue to undergo monitoring through an annual retention program. None of Mandaue City’s barangays has had its drug-cleared status revoked.

The measures include barangay-based programs. Authorities also conduct regular drug testing and continued intervention for individuals who have previously undergone rehabilitation. Authorities refer back for intervention those individuals who test positive again.
He also emphasized that addiction can be a recurring problem. Individuals who complete rehabilitation may still experience an urge to use drugs but can learn to manage that through continued support.

articles.title: ICC prosecution: Verify open-source materials on a case-by-case basis
articles.summary: After the defense team of former President Rodrigo Duterte asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) to require expert verification for open-source materials, the prosecution urged Trial Chamber…

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 6:24pm

After the defense team of former President Rodrigo Duterte asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) to require expert verification for open-source materials, the prosecution urged Trial Chamber III to reject the request, saying the need for such verification should be determined on a case-by-case basis.
In a document dated September 9 and posted on the ICC website, ad interim Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang opposed the defense’s request to amend the E-Court Protocol.

“Open-source and user-generated evidence are extremely broad categories of documents that capture numerous types of evidence. As such, whether open-source or user-generated evidence requires an accompanying expert report should be determined on case-by-case basis by the submitting party that has the burden of establishing its relevance, probative value and assessing its potential prejudicial effect,” Niang said.
“It is unreasonable, unnecessary and against the interests of judicial efficiency, to require an expert report to accompany all forms of open-source and user-generated evidence,” he added.
On September 4, Duterte’s defense team asked the ICC chamber to amend the E-Court Protocol regarding open-source materials.
Duterte’s counsel Peter Haynes argued that the prosecution’s evidence had ballooned since the charges were confirmed, increasing from around 5,000 items to 25,000.

Haynes said the evidence reviewed by the defense so far was of “poor quality,” alleging that some were duplicates. He also said that, amid rampant “fake news” surrounding the case, merely providing a URL was not enough to verify the authenticity of an item of evidence.
“The Defense is deeply concerned that the quality and quantity of the evidence in this case risks flooding the record with unreliable and/or irrelevant material,” Haynes said.

“It is proposed that such expert verification reports, which can cover multiple items of evidence, should always accompany open source and user-generated evidence submitted to the Chamber in the present case,” he added.

Niang, however, said the defense’s proposed amendment would require an expert report for all forms of open-source materials. Given the broad range of materials that may fall under the category, he said the need for expert verification should instead be assessed separately for each item.

For example, publicly available reports from organizations such as the United Nations and Human Rights Watch, as well as reputable news publications, should not automatically require expert evidence, Niang said.
“Chambers of this Court have consistently allowed the submission of open-source evidence of this nature without the need for an accompanying expert report,” Niang said.

The prosecution acknowledged that the court must remain vigilant in assessing open-source material amid the rise of artificial intelligence and online disinformation, but said the response should be proportionate to the risks. — VBL, GMA News

Detained pastor Apollo Quiboloy has lodged libel complaints against Senator Risa Hontiveros and House lawmakers Akbayan Partylist Representative Perci Cendaña and ML Partylist Representative Leila de Lima.
The lawmakers confirmed the complaints in separate statements.

Hontiveros, who oversaw the Senate hearings that brought forward Quiboloy’s alleged victims, said that she was not afraid of anything, adding that Quiboloy should face the cases filed against him instead of trying to turn the discussion on its head.
Quiboloy is accused of heavy crimes such as human trafficking, sexual abuse and child abuse, said Hontiveros.

“Ang dapat nating protektahan ay ang mga biktima at kababayan nating naglakas-loob magsalita at lumantad laban kay Quiboloy. Hangga’t humihingi sila ng hustisya, tatayo ako sa tabi nila,” Hontiveros said in a statement on Thursday.
(The ones we should protect are the victims and our countrymen that were brave and came forward against Quiboloy. As long as they seek justice, I stand next to them.)
Meanwhile, De Lima said that the cyber libel case is misdirecting the issue. Quiboloy must answer for his crimes, she added.

“Let us not waste government resources for this baseless case. Huwag na silang magkunwari na biktima siya ng cyber libel. Apollo Quiboloy is not a victim. Ipagtanggol na lang niya ang kanyang sarili sa kanyang mga kaso sa mga karumaldumal na krimen na panggagahasa at pagturing sa mga kababaihan bilang mga personal na kagamitan,” De Lima said.

(Let us not waste government resources for this baseless case. They should not act like victims of cyber libel. Apollo Quiboloy is not a victim. He should defend himself from his grievous crimes such as rape and treating women like personal objects.)
Cendaña said that it was an “honor” to be named alongside Hontiveros and De Lima in Quiboloy’s suit.

In a statement on Thursday, the Akbayan Partylist called the charges “laughable.”

“Quiboloy enjoys being called all sorts of ridiculous things, but not things grounded in facts. Akbayan stands by the victims’ testimonies and the legal records in the Philippines and the United States,” the partylist said.
Quiboloy is currently detained at the Pasig City Jail Male Dormitory facing charges of qualified human trafficking and sexual abuse.

articles.title: Amid Visayas rotational brownouts, House inquiry sought
articles.summary: Cebu 3rd District Rep. Karen Hope F. Garcia has called for an urgent House inquiry on the power situation in the Visayas, amidst shortage of electricity and implementation of rotational brownouts.…

blocks.text: LAPU-LAPU CITY, Cebu — Cebu 3rd District Rep. Karen Hope F. Garcia has called for an urgent House inquiry on the power situation in the Visayas, amidst shortage of electricity and implementation of rotational brownouts.
Garcia also wants to evaluate their direct impact on power pricing.

On Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, Garcia filed House Bill 1439 urging the House Committee on Energy to summon officials from the Department of Energy (DOE), the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC), the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP), and major generation and distribution utilities to present an unvarnished assessment of the power crisis.

Currently, Cebu and other provinces have been plagued with brownouts, with data from the NGCP showing that the Visayas Grid has been under chronic strain, logging 94 yellow alerts and 31 red alerts as of September 4, with additional alerts declared until today.
Looming power price hikes
Recent reports also state that Cebu’s electricity rates could spike from roughly ₱11 to nearly ₱19 per kilowatt-hour.

The lawmaker wants the legislative inquiry to uncover the real operational status of power plants across the region and determine whether systems failures are being unfairly passed on to consumers through inflated power bills.

She raised serious concerns over recent projections, indicating that households could see their power rates jump by as much as 70 percent following short-term procurement decisions made during recent power deficits.
“The public deserves complete transparency and accountability,” Garcia said.
She argued that ordinary families are effectively being treated as a financial safety cushion for planning deficiencies and power supply breakdowns.
Mechanical failures?

The inquiry will require the DOE and key stakeholders to present a detailed, unit-by-unit outage history of power plants in the Visayas grid to verify if plant breakdowns are legitimate mechanical failures. It also aims to tackle DOE findings on generation facilities and whether show-cause orders or penalties have been issued against non-compliant operators.

Garcia also wants the Energy Regulatory Commission to explore whether distribution utilities can apply for deferred recovery of generation costs or other relief measures to protect consumers from sudden bill shock.
“We need to establish the ground truth behind these blackouts,” Garcia said.

articles.title: Bayeux Tapestry goes on display at sold-out London exhibit
articles.summary: The nearly 1,000 year-old, 70-meter-long tapestry is considered a symbol of UK-France friendship. More than 100,000 tickets have been sold.

image.caption: The Bayeux Tapestry will be on display in London until next JulyImage: Suzanne Plunkett/REUTERS

blocks.text: The Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London opened Thursday to much fanfare, in what British newspaper the Times has dubbed "Tapestry-mania," with more than 100,000 tickets already sold.

The tapestry is on loan from France, and comes after years of diplomacy, with the move being seen as a symbol of close ties between Paris and London. It is thought to be the first time the tapestry has gone on display outside of France.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called the tapestry's loan a "return," while King Charles III hailed the move as a "precious symbol of trust at a time when trust seems sadly to be in short supply between nations."
The work is believed to have been made in England nearly 1,000 years ago before finding its way to Bayeux, now located in the French region of Normandy.

Two previous attempts to loan the Bayeux Tapestry to the UK were unsuccessful. Once was in 1953 for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II, and again in 1966 for the 900th anniversary of the Battle of Hastings, which is depicted on the tapestry.

blocks.caption: King Charles III, Queen Camilla alongside France's President Emmanuel Macron at a preview event in LondonImage: Adrian Dennis/AFP

blocks.text: What is the Bayeux Tapestry?
The Bayeux Tapestry is a 70-meter long artwork, which is thought to be incomplete, depicting the Norman conquest of England in 1066.

Norman forces led by William the Conqueror were able to defeat and dethrone King Harold Godwinson in a campaign culminating in victory at the Battle of Hastings. The tapestry famously depicts Harold being shot in the eye with an arrow, as he is said to have died — admittedly in what modern historians believe is likely a myth or artistic exaggeration.

This conquest was a crucial contributing moment in the establishment of what would become England and later the British Empire and the UK. It was the last of several successful foreign invasions of England in a millennium, and turned out to be the last one for a millennium

blocks.caption: The Bayeux Tapestry is thought to be nearly 1,000 years old Image: Pascal Deloche/Godong/picture alliance

blocks.text: The conquest also added the final core ingredient, French, to the linguistic melting pot that produced the modern English language.

The embroidered cloth, which has brief Latin titles captioning its 58 scenes, is widely accepted to have been made in England as a tribute to William after his victory. It was then transported to his family home in Normandy.
The Bayeux Tapestry will be on display at London's British Museum until next July.

articles.title: Nearly 2 in 3 Pinoys back COA order for VP Sara to return P73 million — poll
articles.summary: The survey found that most Filipinos want the disallowed P73 million confidential funds to be returned.

blocks.text: September 10, 2026 | 6:08pm
Members of the prosecution team present boxes labeled “Confidential Funds” during the 11th day of the Senate impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte in Pasay City on Aug. 3, 2026.
Senate of the Philippines via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — A recent survey found that nearly two in every three Filipinos want Vice President Sara Duterte to return the P73.28 million in disallowed confidential funds to the government.

Based on the latest results of The National Momentum Survey by Momentum Research, 64% of Filipinos say they agree or strongly agree with the Commission on Audit (COA) order that obliged Duterte to return the allegedly misused funds.
In 2024, COA issued a notice of disallowance on part of the 2022 OVP confidential funds after it found that the funds were spent on activities that are unrelated to their declared purposes.
Only 24% said they disagree or strongly disagree, 8.9% said they are unsure, and 3.1% refused to answer.
Younger gen want the funds back
The survey found that, in terms of age, most of those who believed that Duterte should comply with the COA order came from the younger generation.
“Almost 4 in 5 Gen Zs believe the vice president should comply with the COA order, while 3 in 5 Millennials share the same view,” the survey read.
Most of the respondents from Generation X, or 56.1%, also believed that the allegedly misused confidential funds should be returned to the state.

Meanwhile, it was also observed that 52.7% of respondents belonging to the Baby Boomers and the Silent Generation backed the COA order, which “do not show a clear majority in support considering the margin of error” according to the survey.

The National Momentum Survey was carried out through face-to-face interviews with 1,487 adults across the country from August 18 to 23, with a ±2.5 percentage-point national margin of error at a 95% confidence level.

articles.title: [Rappler Investigates] Refuge of the privileged accused
articles.summary: Top officials, including past presidents charged with plunder and/or graft and corruption, suddenly fell ill or developed illnesses that merited confinement

blocks.text: You’ve probably noticed, just as we have, that there’s a common playbook being passed around by government officials facing imminent arrest or a string of legal cases. It’s finding refuge in a hospital after raising a variety of illnesses that require medical attention.

Top officials, including past presidents charged with plunder and/or graft and corruption, suddenly fell ill or developed illnesses that merited confinement. It’s not totally surprising for officials used to being accorded special attention and treatment to suddenly develop heart ailments, if not hypertension.

Researcher Lourence Marcellana reviewed the past two decades and found at least eight top officials — top, mind you, not even lower-ranking — who either sought prolonged hospital stay or temporary relief in hospitals before or during detention.

No one admitted, but many suspected, that the hospital admissions especially for the likes of former speaker Martin Romualdez — who went straight to a hospital before an arrest warrant could be served — might have been a means to delay the inevitable: imprisonment.

But assuming good faith and authentic health needs, Southern Illinois University criminology associate professor Raymund Narag pointed out in his piece: “Medical considerations… have appeared selectively available to the rich and powerful.” Whatever criteria were applied to Romualdez should likewise “apply to thousands of poor Filipinos now languishing in overcrowded jails nationwide.”

These Filipinos have been no match, too, for the likes of former presidents Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo (who had neck issues) and Joseph Estrada (knees), or even senators Jinggoy Estrada, Rodante Marcoleta, and Juan Ponce Enrile, former first lady Imelda Marcos (recently acquitted by the Supreme Court on seven counts of graft), and former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan, who all raised a garden variety of health issues.
To their credit, Bong Revilla, Jinggoy Estrada, Marcoleta, and Bonoan went to authorities first before eventually finding their way to hospitals.

These latest developments threatened to eclipse major investigations by our tech writer Gelo Gonzales, with the assistance of Lance Bustos, about this appalling, perhaps unknown-to-many forum that exploits women. I will alert you early on that this is gated content (reading the full story will require payment or membership in Rappler+) to support the journalism that we do.

This online community boasts of having 430,000 registered members who share intimate photos and videos of women, many without their consent, involving manipulation and deceit. Content is shared as if they were conquests of victimized women — mirroring repulsive behavior of the male species. Read the first part.
Part 2 discusses how abuse is rewarded financially at the expense of the victims. The forum has thrived because of challenges that face regulation and jurisdiction.

Since we published the stories, we have received emails that provide tips and more information about this exploitative forum. Gelo is in the process of compiling these reports for possible follow-up stories. If you have information to share, email us at investigative@rappler.com.

Another project we’ve been working on involves political dynasties. If you’ve been keen observers of Philippine politics, you will agree that the pattern of corruption in government is also partly enabled by the continuing domination of the same political families that just shift terms and positions among themselves.

Power remains locked within the family with little check-and-balance and ultimate accountability. It’s incredible how the same surnames surface every campaign period, leaving voters with little choice but to narrow their options of who to vote into office.
This is a running series all the way to October when we commemorate the 35th anniversary of the Local Government Code. Here’s what we have published so far, with more in the pipeline:

items: The Dutertes’ 40-year reign: Forged from strongman and victim
The Pinedas of Pampanga: A dynasty by succession
Centuries in the making: Singsons’ unrivaled power in Ilocos Sur
How the Romualdezes held their political grip on Leyte for generations
When you see the Ynares name, you know you’re in Rizal

blocks.text: We continue to keep track of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte that has run for 23 days now. The latest issue on the table is the voting threshold, with Senator Erwin Tulfo seeking clarification on how many votes will be required for either a conviction or acquittal of the Vice President.

Will it be two-thirds of the 24 senators? Or will it be two-thirds of the senators who are present — just 20 at the present time because of the continuing absence of four senators: Marcoleta and Estrada, who are detained on plunder charges; Loren Legarda, who remains on extended medical leave; and Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, still a fugitive.

The impeachment court is seeking the opinion of amici curiae, friends of the court, who will likely include retired Supreme Court justices, to help them settle the question. A decision is expected by September 23. Check out the adjusted schedule of the impeachment court here.
Till Thursday after next!

blocks.text: "My brother did leave behind an heir to the throne, and that was very clearly stated," she said, accusing those behind the announcement on Wednesday night of creating "confusion and turmoil" while the family was still grieving.

Meanwhile the late king's mother, Queen Best Kemigisa, has said royal guards have been withdrawn from the palace and soldiers deployed, restricting the royal family's movement and their ability to receive visitors, describing the situation as "house arrest".
She appealed to the army's leadership and President Yoweri Museveni to allow the family to mourn and bury Oyo in peace on Saturday.
"I appeal to those fighting over the throne: please, there will be time for all of that," she said. "Let us grieve and bury my son King Oyo."
Thousands of mourners are expected to attend the burial at the royal tombs near the palace in Fort Portal in western Uganda.
His body was returned to Uganda from the US on Friday, and preparations for the funeral are under way.
Tooro is one of Uganda's traditional kingdoms. Its monarch has no formal political authority but remains an important cultural figure in western Uganda.
Uganda abolished its traditional kingdoms in 1967, but they were restored in the 1990s under President Museveni. Their monarchs are recognised as cultural leaders rather than political rulers.
The existence of Oyo's son was first publicly revealed in the days after the king's death by President Museveni, who said he had been told about the young boy by the queen mother.
No other details have officially been disclosed, and he had not previously been presented as Oyo's heir.
The disagreement has exposed the complicated way in which succession works in Tooro.
Unlike Britain's monarchy, where the crown passes according to an established line of succession, Tooro's monarch is chosen from the Babiito, the royal dynastic clan.

At a press conference in ​the kingdom's capital of Fort Portal, the royal clan's succession committee announced Kijanangoma, Oyo's cousin and a news presenter ​at the state-run broadcaster UBC, as monarch.
The clan elders said they had the customary authority to choose a suitable prince to become "the Omukama" - the local title for the king of Tooro.
The succession panel said it had carried out "due diligence, consultation and adequate consideration" before selecting Kijanangoma, with 19 members signing the resolution.
Kijanangoma is the son of Prince Christopher Paul Kijanangoma and a grandson of former Tooro king George David Rukidi III.
Another royal, UK-based Prince George Desmond Kamurasi, was initially considered for the throne but declined, citing other responsibilities, according to the succession committee.
It is not yet clear when the enthronement will take place, but the committee said it would be conducted in accordance with the traditions and customs of the Tooro kingdom.

“However, considering that the hearing on the said accused’s manifestation and urgent motion has not yet been terminated today and will continue tomorrow, September 11, 2026, his confinement at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center will remain until further orders from the court,” Sandiganbayan 3rd Division Clerk of Court Dennis Pulma told reporters on Thursday, September 10.

Romualdez was arrested inside his hospital room in San Juan City, but the police could not move him to the court or jail because of his medical condition. He also filed a motion with the court to remain under hospital confinement, further delaying his detention.

blocks.text: The 3rd Division had set a hearing on Romualdez’s motion on Thursday morning.

“An Order of Commitment (Pending Trial) dated September 10, 2026 was issued by the court on even date for the detention/commitment of accused Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez at the BJMP (Bureau of Jail Management and Penology)-Male Dormitory, in Payatas, Quezon City,” said Pulma.

articles.title: 8 school sites, 406 artesian wells eyed as El Niño backup
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Eight public school properties and 406 artesian wells are being eyed as potential backup water sources here for prolonged dry conditions linked to El Niño. The City Council…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Eight public school properties and 406 artesian wells are being eyed as potential backup water sources here for prolonged dry conditions linked to El Niño.

The City Council has urged the city government to pursue alternative and supplementary water sources, including the possible revival of groundwater development in eight city-owned school properties in coordination with the Department of Education (DepEd) Cebu City Division and the Metropolitan Cebu Water District (MCWD).

This comes as the city prepares for the possible intensification of El Niño and the resulting pressure on water supplies, with the council also declaring Cebu City in a state of preparedness for the phenomenon.

Councilor Dave Tumulak sponsored the measure, which calls on Mayor Nestor Archival to identify feasible alternative sources and establish water-supply contingencies to ensure adequate and continuous supply during prolonged dry conditions.
The council’s action follows a Sept. 8 El Niño preparedness summit where city officials discussed existing and potential water sources, including artesian wells, deep wells, and rainwater harvesting.
Eight school properties
The council previously passed a resolution on Aug. 4 requesting DepEd Cebu City and MCWD to consider reviving a proposed groundwater development project within eight city-owned school properties.
The sites are the following:

items: Barrio Luz Elementary School along Archbishop Reyes Ave.
Labangon Elementary School on Katipunan St.
Don Vicente Rama High School in Basak
Bulacao Community High School in Bulacao
Pardo Elementary School on A. Gabuya St.
Quiot Elementary School on F. Sabellano St.
Punta Princesa Elementary School on Tres de Abril St.
Talamban Elementary School in Talamban

blocks.text: The resolution also asks the city government, DepEd, and MCWD to explore a possible tripartite agreement for the project.
Any groundwater development, however, remains subject to technical, legal, and administrative evaluation, as well as existing laws, rules, and regulations.

This means the eight school properties do not yet represent an additional water supply for the city. Their potential as groundwater sources still needs to undergo assessment before any development can proceed.
406 artesian wells
The school sites are not the only potential sources under consideration.
During the Sept. 8 El Niño Summit 2026, Engineer Paul Gelasque, head of the Department of Public Services (DPS), presented the role of the 406 artesian wells in the water supply during droughts.
The wells could supplement the city’s water supply when MCWD sources decline during prolonged dry spells, particularly in upland and interior barangays that could experience water scarcity earlier.
The city said, however, that the wells would need proper maintenance and rehabilitation to maximize their potential as alternative sources.
The 406 wells, therefore, represent an existing resource that the city can assess for possible augmentation rather than a guaranteed additional supply that can immediately replace MCWD sources.
The Sept. 8 summit sought to map available water resources and coordinate contingency measures among city offices as part of the city’s preparation for El Niño.
Other water sources in Cebu City
The City Council also passed a separate resolution on Aug. 18 urging MCWD to seriously consider the feasibility of developing other identified water sources around Cebu City.

These include sources in Gibuthan, Upper Udlon, the boundary of Barangays Tabunan and Taptap, Sitio Tagaytay in Barangay Adlaon, Buot-Bonbon River, Mangyapyap Falls in Barangay Paril, and the water impounding facility in Barangay Pamutan.

articles.title: PH, South Korea partner for 1,500 new firetrucks - DILG
articles.summary: The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said on Thursday that it will deploy 1,500 firetrucks nationwide next year through an agreement with South Korea.

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 5:38pm
The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said on Thursday that it will deploy 1,500 firetrucks nationwide next year through an agreement with South Korea.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the firetrucks will be acquired through a government-to-government agreement with South Korea.
The DILG, the Office of the President, Department of Foreign Affairs, and Bureau of Fire Protection are coordinating with the South Korean government for the acquisition, he added.
“Within one and a half years, kumpleto na lahat ang munisipyo, wala na tayong magiging problema. Kumpleto na sa buong Pilipinas," said Remulla in a statement.
(Within one and a half years, every municipality will be fully equipped, and we won't have any more problems. It will be complete across the entire Philippines.)
“This is the cleanest transaction that is possible with the best possible benefit sa lahat ng mga Pilipino."
(This is the cleanest transaction possible, bringing the best possible benefit to all Filipinos.)
Meanwhile, the DILG turned over 20 Class 1 Unified 911 emergency response motorcycles to Police Regional Office 6 at Camp General Martin Teofilo B. Delgado in Iloilo City.
Of the 20 motorcycles, 10 were given to the Aklan Police Provincial Office and 10 others were turned over to the Iloilo City Police Office.
The DILG said the motorcycles will reinforce the emergency response following the rollout of the Unified 911.
The department said the system relies on geolocation to route callers to local emergency teams who can converse in the area's native language.
"Lahat ng mga language na ’yan, kung saan ka naroroon, kapag na-geotag ang tawag ninyo, ang sasagot sa inyo ay ang local language na," said Remulla.
(All of those languages—wherever you are located, once your call is geotagged, the person who answers will speak the local language.) —Vince Angelo Ferreras/RF, GMA News

articles.title: 'People were trampling me': Philippine ferry fire survivor recalls narrow escape
articles.summary: A survivor has told the BBC of the chaos onboard as the ferry caught fire near the popular tourist spot of Coron.

blocks.text: Passengers on board a ferry to the Philippines' Palawan province were jolted into chaos on Wednesday night, when a fire broke out on the vessel.
Frantic cries pierced the night sky as hot air filled the boat, recalls Roland Lerma, one of more than 100 passengers aboard the MV June Aster.

Five people have died and 86 people are missing after the fire, which, in a country where shipping accidents are not uncommon, could become one of the deadliest maritime disasters the Philippines has seen.
Families are anxiously awaiting news about their loved ones on board, while survivors like Lerma are coming to terms with their harrowing escape.
Speaking to the BBC from a hospital in Coron, Lerma recalled that as the fire spread and he scrambled to get off the burning boat, he slipped and fell.
"When I was on the floor, people were trampling me," said the 30-year-old.
He started crawling until he could find his footing again, before leaping off the vessel into the sea.
He said he saw children who had also jumped in the water, though he could not make out their faces in the dark.
"When I hit the water, I ditched all my possessions - the clothes I was wearing, phones, bags - so that I could float," he said.
Lerma said he floated on his back for about two hours before rescuers arrived and pulled him and other survivors out of the water.
"It was cold. If the rescue had been delayed, I would have definitely died last night," he said.

Lerma, who works in construction, is from Leyte province. He had travelled to the capital Manila with five of his neighbours, where they boarded the ferry to bring them to work at Coron, a popular tourist spot in Palawan province.

According to the Philippine Coast Guard, the MV June Aster departed Manila's Port of Baseco on Tuesday night at 20:13 local time (12:13 GMT) and was scheduled to arrive at the Coron port at 18:00 on Wednesday.
But the ferry caught fire just 1.2 nautical miles (2.2km) off the coast of Coron's Marcilla village.
The fire was first reported at 18:45 local time on Wednesday night by a staff member of Atienza Shipping Lines, which owns the boat, the Coast Guard said.
The company said in a statement on Thursday that it was co-operating fully with authorities and expressed "profound sadness" about the fire.
Authorities say a survivor had told them the flames had started in the cargo hold after a loud explosion.
The ship had been carrying several motorcycles, an electric car, a forklift, a pick-up van and other goods, the Philippine Coast Guard said.
As the journey was expected to take more than 20 hours, passengers had slept on bunk beds onboard overnight.
Lerma said that two Chileans - a couple who looked like they were in their late 20s or early 30s - had slept in the beds next to his.
Authorities have since confirmed that two Chilean nationals were among the 43 people rescued.

Lerma and two of his neighbours are now in a hospital in Coron. Another person in their group has been taken to a bigger hospital in the neighbouring island of Culion, while two others remain missing, Lerma says.
"I have a couple of bruises and my chest is still hurting," Lerma said. "Last night, I had a hard time breathing. But I am okay now."
Search and rescue operations are ongoing, though authorities say the fire on the MV June Aster has still not been put out and there was visible smoke from the ferry.
A spokesperson for the Philippine Coast Guard said in a local television interview many of the survivors "are still in shock".
Meanwhile, families of the ferry's missing passengers are enduring an agonising wait.
Anelyn Magbanua told the BBC that her husband Marlon was on the ferry. He was returning to Coron after visiting Manila to see two of their children who are studying at the capital.
"He spent a couple of days there. He even sent me their pictures," she said.
She last heard from him while the ferry was passing through a village about two hours from the port in Coron.
Magbanua and her two-year-old son had gone to bed early on Wednesday night expecting Marlon to be home soon.
But she was woken up later that night by a relative who informed her that her husband's ferry had caught fire.
On Thursday she rushed to the hospital when she heard there was a chance her husband might be one of the rescued survivors there.
But officials have since told her that Marlon remains unaccounted for.
"My two-year-old son and I are outside the hospital as we speak. We have nothing but ourselves," she told the BBC over the phone.
"I can't describe what I am feeling right now. I have been crying and praying since last night."

articles.title: Manibela to hold transport strike on Sept. 14, 2026 amid rising fuel prices
articles.summary: Transport group Manibela on Thursday announced that it will hold a nationwide transport strike on Monday, September 14 due to the rising fuel prices.

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 5:33pm
Transport group Manibela on Thursday announced that it will hold a nationwide transport strike on Monday, September 14 due to the rising fuel prices.
"Nationwide transport strike September 14, 2026! Dahil sa taas presyo ng krudo at gasolina dahil inutil ang DOE!" the group said in a Facebook post.
(Nationwide transport strike on September 14, 2026! Due to rising crude oil and gasoline prices because the Department of Energy is useless!)
Firms this week hiked prices per liter of gasoline by P4.69, diesel by P5.18, and kerosene by P5.58.

The Department of Energy explained that the ongoing tensions between the US and Iran have resulted in the fuel price increases. It added that the weakening of the Philippine peso against the American dollar was also a factor.
While the week is not yet over, pump prices of petroleum products are expected to rise for the second straight week next Tuesday, based on movements in global prices.

According to an oil industry source, gasoline prices could rise by P2.00 to P4.00 per liter, and diesel by P3.00 to P5.00 per liter, based on the average Mean of Platts Singapore (MOPS) and foreign exchange trading from September 7 to September 9. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: SEA Games medalist Fajardo trains with Donaire Sr. for pro boxing debut
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Cebuano former international amateur boxing standout Mark Ashley Fajardo has begun his training camp with Sanman Boxing in General Santos City as he prepares for his…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Cebuano former international amateur boxing standout Mark Ashley Fajardo has begun his training camp with Sanman Boxing in General Santos City as he prepares for his much-anticipated professional debut in October.

Fajardo recently trained under veteran boxing coach Nonito Donaire Sr., the father of former four-division world champion Nonito “Filipino Flash” Donaire Jr. Donaire Sr. is now one of the main trainers at Sanman Boxing.
Fajardo also received guidance from former interim world champion Reymart Gaballo.
He announced his decision to turn professional a month ago,after a promising amateur career highlighted by international medals.
SEA Games medalist turned pro boxer
The 2025 Southeast Asian Games bronze medalist is now training full-time under Donaire Sr. and fellow Sanman trainer Dondon Jimenea ahead of his pro debut.
Fajardo won the bronze medal in the men’s 69-kilogram division at the 2025 SEA Games in Thailand. He lost to host fighter Bunjong Sinsiri via unanimous decision in the semifinals.

He also captured a bronze medal at the 2024 Asian Boxing Confederation (ASBC) Asian U22 and Youth Boxing Championships in Kazakhstan. That further established him as one of the country’s promising amateur boxers.
Fajardo now begins a new chapter in his career as a professional, using the moniker “The Hitman.” He turned pro alongside fellow Cebuano Jay Bryan Baricuatro of Talisay City.

articles.title: We Belong in the Room: Filipino Youth in Global Spaces
articles.summary: For many young Filipinos, international opportunities can feel out of reach. They can seem reserved for people with extensive experience,

blocks.text: For many young Filipinos, international opportunities can feel out of reach. They can seem reserved for people with extensive experience, impressive credentials, or the financial means to participate. Sometimes, the biggest barrier is simply believing that we belong there.
I know that feeling.
So when I applied to the Universal Youth Leadership Summit (UYLS) 2026 in Bali, Indonesia, part of me questioned whether I was qualified enough to enter that space. I applied anyway.

From August 20 to 23, 2026, I had the opportunity to represent the Philippines as a fully funded delegate at UYLS 2026. Organized by Universal Youth Movement, the summit brought together around 50 young people from more than 20 countries under the theme “Sustainable Futures,” with discussions on leadership, green innovation, climate action, and mental wellbeing.

As my third international summit, I once again found myself in a room filled with young people from different cultures, communities, and experiences. But more than the discussions themselves, the experience reminded me of something important:
Filipino youth belong in global spaces.
Not because we need to prove that we are just as capable as young people from other countries, but because we already have perspectives, experiences, and ideas worth bringing to the table.
More Than Representation

At the summit, group discussions often challenged me to reconsider ideas I thought I already understood. A delegate would share an experience from their country, and suddenly an issue I viewed from one perspective had another dimension.
These conversations reinforced how global issues are rarely experienced equally.

Climate change may be a global problem, but its effects are shaped by geography, resources, governance, and inequality. The same can be said about education, mental wellbeing, and access to opportunities.
This is precisely why Filipino youth need to be part of these conversations.

We come from communities that have their own realities, challenges, and solutions. We understand what it means to live in a country vulnerable to climate disasters while navigating persistent inequalities. We have experiences that can enrich global conversations, not perspectives we need to leave behind before entering them.

The summit also went beyond the traditional conference setting. We participated in a beach clean-up at Jerman Beach in Kuta and attended a panel discussion on mental wellbeing at Politeknik Negeri Bali. These activities allowed us to engage with the community while learning alongside other delegates.

Even in informal conversations, cultural exchange became part of the experience. We were not simply delegates representing different countries. We were young people comparing realities, asking questions, sharing stories, and learning from one another.
Going Global, Bringing the Philippines With Us
My experience also changed how I understand the phrase “going global.”
Going global does not mean leaving the Philippines behind.
It means bringing the Philippines with us.
It means sharing our perspectives, culture, experiences, and realities with people from other countries, and returning home with lessons, connections, and ideas that can benefit our own communities.
International opportunities can sometimes become individual achievements: a certificate, a line on a resume, or a photograph taken abroad. But their value should extend beyond the individual.
When young Filipinos enter these spaces, we also expand the imagination of what other Filipino youth believe is possible for themselves.

That matters because many young people may never apply for opportunities like UYLS because they assume they cannot afford them, are not experienced enough, or simply are not the kind of person these programs are looking for.
I had those doubts, too.
But young people should not only be given opportunities because they are already confident, accomplished, or well-connected. They should also be given spaces where they can become those things.
The World Needs Filipino Youth

We are often told that young people are the leaders of tomorrow. But Filipino youth are already contributing today: organizing communities, advocating for causes, conducting research, creating art, building businesses, and engaging with issues that extend beyond our borders.
What we need is not permission to have something valuable to say.
We need more opportunities to say it.

My experience in Bali reminded me that I can enter a global space without leaving my identity at the door. I can bring my experiences, my questions, my culture, and the realities of the community I come from.
And I can return home ready to share what I have learned.
After every international opportunity, I find myself asking: What can I bring back? Who can I inspire? And how can I use what I learned to contribute to my community?
Perhaps these are questions more Filipino youth should be encouraged to ask.

Because the goal should not simply be to send Filipino youth abroad. It should be to build a generation confident enough to enter global spaces, contribute meaningfully, and return home ready to create change.
We go global not to leave the Philippines behind, but to bring the Philippines with us.

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Cebu’s volleyball stars will get a chance to shine on their home turf as the Premier Volleyball League (PVL) brings its 10th season grand opening to the SM Seaside Arena Cebu on October 10.

The historic season opener will feature two matches showcasing some of the country’s top players, including several homegrown Cebuana talents who will make their homecoming in front of a 16,000-capacity crowd.

The Choco Mucho Flying Titans will open the doubleheader against the Capital1 Solar Spikers at 1 p.m., with Cebuana standouts Cherry “Sisi” Rondina, Isa Molde, and Deanna Wong leading the charge for the Flying Titans.

Rondina, a native of Compostela in northern Cebu, remains one of the country’s most recognizable volleyball players. She recently added another international achievement to her résumé after teaming up with Bernadeth Pons to win the women’s beach volleyball gold medal at last year’s Southeast Asian Games in Thailand.

Wong, a native of Minglanilla, will provide the Flying Titans with her trademark playmaking as one of the PVL’s premier setters. Teaming up with them is Isa Molde, a product of Catmon Integrated School under teacher-coach Vilma Veloso, a multiple Palarong Pambansa gold medalist who has helped develop several volleyball talents from northern Cebu.
They will face a familiar Cebuano connection in Capital1 rookie Khy Cepada who happens to be also a product of Veloso’s volleyball program in Catmon.
Smashers vs Chargers
The second match, scheduled for 6 p.m., will pit the Creamline Cool Smashers against the Akari Chargers.
Creamline will feature rookie combine standout Barbie Jamili of Liloan, Cebu, who will make her PVL debut on the biggest volleyball stage in her home province.
Jamili will be joined by Cebu-based volleyball standout Dij Rodriguez, a former Southwestern University (SWU) Lady Cobra who was born in Dumaguete City.
Akari, meanwhile, will parade another product of Veloso’s volleyball program in veteran Gretchel Soltones, who also hails from Catmon.
Decade of growth

The Cebu opening is particularly fitting as the PVL and Spikers’ Turf mark their 10th anniversary, celebrating a decade of growth that has helped expand volleyball’s reach and popularity across the country.
Preparations are already underway for the season-opening festivities at the SM Seaside Arena Cebu, which broke ground in 2021 and opened to the public last July.
Bringing the PVL’s milestone season opener to Cebu also highlights the province’s long-standing contribution to Philippine volleyball.
Cebu has consistently produced elite players, promising prospects and coaches who have helped shape the sport at the national level.

Among the other PVL players with Cebuano roots are Choco Mucho’s Isa Molde of Catmon, Galeries Tower’s Dimdim Pacres, Farm Fresh players Lorene Toring and Pierre Abellana, Nxled’s Krich Macaslang, and PLDT’s Shiela Kiseo and Zenneth Perolino, among others.
