articles.title: Dustin Yu addresses resurfaced online exchange with gay adult content creator
articles.summary: Dustin Yu broke his silence on a past online exchange with an LGBTQ+ adult content creator that recently resurfaced online and stirred speculation. The exchange took place in December 2021, before…

blocks.text: Dustin Yu broke his silence on a past online exchange with an LGBTQ+ adult content creator that recently resurfaced online and stirred speculation.

The exchange took place in December 2021, before Twitter was rebranded as X. In a now-deleted post, Yu replied “OTW (on the way)” to a message from the content creator that read, “andito po ko sa bahay charot.”
Yu took to X on Thursday, Sept. 10, to clarify the context behind his old comment after it resurfaced on the platform.
“I’m doing a film right now, nasa lock-in taping ako and walang halos signal. I was told that I’m being dragged regarding something I commented years ago,” the 25-year-old actor said.
Yu explained that he initially chose not to address the issue, but wanted to clarify his position.
“I decided to speak up for the sake of my loved ones, while making sure to do so with respect for the LGBT community,” expressed the actor.
“I replied to a comment on that account maybe around 5 years ago as a joke and simply to interact with people who were tagging me. Wala akong ibang intention behind it,” he added.
Yu also said he only recently learned that the account had changed its account name and content.

“Ngayon ko lang nalaman na nagpalit na pala ng account at content ‘yung account na ‘yun, and unfortunately, may mga taong ginagamit ngayon ‘yung old comment ko para gawan ng ibang storya at i-drag ako,” he said.

Hi! I’m doing a film right now, nasa lock-in taping ako and walang halos signal. I was told that I’m being dragged regarding something I commented years ago. Nung una, I didn’t really mind cos I’m more focused on the good days, plus I’m very much happy with my life right now. But…— Dustin Yu (@dustinyuu) September 9, 2026
The actor maintained that his original comment had no other meaning despite interpretations of netizens.
“I know what I meant when I said it, and I won’t let someone twist an old interaction into something it was never meant to be,” Yu said.
Yu ended his statement by urging people to be more positive and kind, particularly when discussing matters that could affect another person.
“We may not always agree or understand each other, but I hope we can choose to be kinder instead of creating stories that can hurt someone,” he said.
“I hope you find happiness that doesn’t have to come at someone else’s expense,” Yu concluded his post.

Yu rose to fame after his stint on “Pinoy Big Brother: Celebrity Collab Edition.” He previously headlined his first Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF) entry “Love You So Bad.” He is set to star in the upcoming movie, “Ba’t Di Na Lang Tayo” opposite on-screen partner Bianca de Vera. /ra

articles.title: Iceland to become first UK high street retailer to open shop in Falkland Islands
articles.summary: Boss Richard Walker is ‘proud to be backing Britain’ with a store in the capital, Stanley

blocks.text: The supermarket chain Iceland has said it will open a shop on the Falkland Islands in early December.
The shop, to be launched in partnership with a local retailer, Kelper Stores, will be the first UK high street brand to have a presence in the British territory and will be in the capital, Stanley.
Richard Walker, the retailer’s executive chair, said the company was “proud to be backing Britain”.

“The Falklands are a special part of the British family and it’s always been an ambition of mine to support it, so being able to bring Iceland to Stanley is a huge moment for us,” Lord Walker said. “This is an important moment for the business and our international aspirations.
“I will personally be visiting the Falklands to officially open the store and I looking forward to welcoming our new customers through the door.”
Iceland’s plan comes less than a week after the Argentine president, Javier Milei, stepped up his nation’s sovereignty claims over the islands.
“Recently, President Trump declared that the US is re-evaluating its historic position in relation to the Malvinas,” Milei said, using the Argentinian name for the Falklands.

He added that the UK was facing “multiple crises of a migratory, demographic and economic nature that are unlikely to be resolved. It is clear that they are on a path of decline. Argentina’s future, however, is flourishing and will prevail.”

Milei also pledged to sanction oil companies drilling in the territory, with this government confirming on Monday that it would file criminal charges against the Israeli energy company Navitas Petroleum and ⁠its executives ⁠for operating ​in the Falklands.

Meanwhile, a local fishing company, Fortuna, and the Danish company F-land ApS have faced local opposition to a joint venture to build a salmon farm in the region, primarily around environmental concerns. Salmon Free Falklands (SFF), set up by local people to oppose the proposal, is calling for a referendum on the project.

articles.title: Sandiganbayan: Romualdez will remain in hospital until further court order
articles.summary: Leyte Representive Martin Romualdez, who is facing a P7.4 billion plunder charge over flood control mess, will remain confined in the Cardinal Santos Medical Center until further orders from the…

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 4:55pm

Leyte Representive Martin Romualdez, who is facing a P7.4 billion plunder charge over flood control mess, will remain confined in the Cardinal Santos Medical Center until further orders from the anti-graft court, Sandiganbayan Third Division Clerk of Court Atty. Dennis Pulma said Thursday.
Pulma said this is because the court is not yet done with its deliberations on Romualdez’s motion seeking hospital confinement in Cardinal Santos due to heart and brain-related illnesses.
“The confinement of former Speaker [Romualdez] in Cardinal Santos will remain until further orders from the court,” Pulma told reporters.
“Doon muna siya (He will stay there for the moment),” he added.

Government prosecutors have alleged that Romualdez received kickbacks from former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co 15 times from 2022 to 2025. Their other co-accused in the case were Jocelyn Sereño, who is working for Romualdez, and Felecito Guevarra, a money changer.
Under BJMP custody

Pulma, however, reiterated that Romualdez is now under the custody of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology because the Sandiganbayan Third Division already issued a commitment order that Romualdez will be detained in New Quezon City jail in Payatas, which is under BJMP’s jurisdiction.
“Being the primary custodian, ang magbabantay roon, the inner circle, are personnel from the BJMP Payatas Male Dormitory,” Pulma said.
Initially, Romualdez was under the custody of the Philippine National Police since September 7 before the anti-graft court issued the commitment order on Thursday, September 10.
Pulma, however, said the police could still be of help to BJMP when it comes to safeguarding Romualdez.

“The police still have a role because the BJMP may seek assistance from the PNP-CIDG (Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group) regarding security concerns or security matters. But the primary custodian [of the former Speaker] are BJMP personnel,” he said.
The Sandiganbayan Third Division has scheduled Day 2 of the hearing on Romualdez’s motion for hospital detention on Friday, September 11.

On Thursday, Cardinal Santos doctors Kurt Sibayan and Rosilio Torres told the anti-graft court that Romualdez’s case was not an emergency, although he remains at high risk for a possible heart attack. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Trump offers $5,000 US to every American if Republicans win midterm elections
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday he would pay every American adult a $5,000 US "Trump dividend" if Republicans retain control of Congress in November's midterm election, an extraordinary…

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump's primetime address at the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, lasted an hour and 45 minutes. (Evan Vucci/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

President Donald Trump said on Wednesday he would pay every American adult a $5,000 US "Trump dividend" if Republicans retain control of Congress in November's midterm election, an extraordinary attempt to persuade voters to back his party.
U.S. president made pitch at Republican Party's midterm convention

Trump made the proposal at his Republican Party's first-ever midterm convention, but it was not immediately clear how the payments would work or whether they would be legal. With approximately 270 million U.S. adults, the idea would cost around $1.35 trillion.

During a primetime address that lasted an hour and 45 minutes, Trump boasted of completing "the greatest two years in the history of the presidency," putting himself squarely at the center of the election despite his deepening unpopularity.

But it was not clear whether his campaign-style speech would appeal to the critical swing voters who opinion polls show have drifted away from Trump's party, amid growing dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the war on Iran.

items: From trade war to midterms: What to watch for this fall
Trump looms over U.S. midterms. Will he help or hurt Republicans?

blocks.text: "We hand America's future to the radical left Democrats, and our nation will spend the next decade just getting back on its feet," he said. "Vote Republicans and we will leave the world in our dust for generations to come."

The two-day Dallas gathering, where Trump will also deliver the closing remarks on Thursday after Vice President JD Vance's keynote address, underscores the extent to which Republicans' fortunes are tethered to Trump and serves as a showcase for their strategy ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
Trump mostly avoids trade war with Canada at GOP convention
The event was so centred on the president that Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters informally dubbed it "Trumpapalooza," a nod to the popular Lollapalooza music festival.

The focus on Trump amounts to a risky bet that he can mobilize the voters who carried him to the presidency two years ago, despite public polls showing his approval ratings have hit an all-time low. The president vowed to pay multiple visits to battleground states and districts in the eight weeks until Election Day.
"I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot," Trump said, a line that may have pleased Democratic campaign strategists just as much as MAGA voters.
Many Republicans skipped convention

The convention presented a tough choice in particular for Republicans facing difficult elections who may need to distance themselves from the president to broaden their appeal but cannot afford to alienate Trump's most committed supporters.

Many such Republicans skipped the convention, including Representative Tom Barrett of Michigan, Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska and Senator Susan Collins of Maine, all facing strong Democratic challengers this fall.

Some, however, elected to travel to Dallas. At least 16 candidates in competitive House and Senate races were scheduled to speak, according to the RNC schedule. Among those who spoke on Wednesday were Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a close Trump ally who is locked in a tough Senate race with Democratic lawmaker James Talarico, and Ohio Senator Jon Husted, who faces former Senator Sherrod Brown.
Though Trump insisted the 21,000-seat arena was "packed," the upper sections remained largely empty during his speech capping Wednesday's program.

articles.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy arrives in Canada seeking air support
articles.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is in the midst of a multi-nation tour to shore up his country's air defenses ahead of winter.

image.caption: Zelenskyy and his wife Olena arrived in Canada in the early hours of ThursdayImage: Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Calgary late on Wednesday for "important meetings ​and agreements" with Canadian officials, including Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Zelenskyy arrived on the heels on attending King Harald V's funeral in Norway, where his plane had been delayed by a drone incursion.
The Ukrainian leader is in the middle of a flurry of trips and meetings to shore up his country's defenses for the cold winter months.
"The main focus will be on supporting Ukraine in protecting our skies and preparing for the winter," Zelenskyy said in a social media post before leaving.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement that the visit "will focus on shared priorities between Canada and Ukraine, including deepening defense, economic, and energy cooperation."
Carney's statement added Canada "remains steadfast in our commitment to support Ukraine's defense, recovery, and reconstruction."
Zelenskyy had also signaled a desire to meet with US President Donald Trump on the matter before the end of September.
Since Russia's invasion in 2022, Moscow has consistently increased attacks on fuel and heating infrastructure in Ukraine in the autumn and winter.
What is happening on the battlefield?

Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery in the Yamalo-Nenets region overnight, as well as a seaport in Dagestan, Zelenskyy said. He added that other unnamed sited critical to Russia's war industry had also been hit.

Alexander Gusev, governor of Russia's Voronezh region, said that one woman in the town of Borisoglebsk had been killed by falling drone debris overnight and that at least 19 drones had been destroyed while flying over the region.
The Russian Defense Ministry said a total of 448 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight.

articles.title: House prosecutors want ex-Sandiganbayan chief to testify in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel has asked the Senate impeachment court to order former Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice Amparo Cabotaje Tang as well as representatives from the Office of the Ombudsman and…

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 4:37pm

The House prosecution panel has asked the Senate impeachment court to order former Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice Amparo Cabotaje Tang as well as representatives from the Office of the Ombudsman and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to testify in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

The prosecution said Tang and the two others will testify on Article 2 of the impeachment case which alleges that the Vice President accumulated unexplained wealth by non-declaration of assets in her wealth statement and failure to divest from businesses even if she was already a public official.

“The testimonies of the foregoing witnesses are material, relevant, and necessary to establish the allegations under Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment, including those concerning unexplained wealth, false Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), and continued business interests,” the House prosecution’s request for subpoena read.

“Justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang (Ret.) will testify on the legal and institutional principles governing public accountability, integrity in public office, and the mechanisms for addressing undisclosed or unexplained wealth and prohibited business interest,” the House prosecution added.

On the other hand, the House prosecution said Atty. Karen Batu of the Office of the Ombudsman will identify and authenticate relevant records maintained by the Office of the Ombudsman, including records pertaining to Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) and related proceedings.

Atty. Gerard Del Rosario of the SEC, for his part, has been enlisted as a witness to will identify and authenticate relevant records of the SEC concerning corporate registrations, ownership or participation, corporate positions, and business interests.
“Their testimonies will likewise cover matters necessarily incidental and relevant thereto,” the House prosecution added.

During the House justice committee hearing on the impeachment complaints against Duterte in April, Batu confirmed that the Vice President did not declare any cash on hand or in bank in her SALN from 2019 to 2014.
“Based on the submitted SALNs, walang nakalagay na cash on hand or deposit (Based on the submitted SALNs, there was none),” Batu said. — RSJ, GMA News

items: Four retired Supreme Court justices will serve as amici curiae in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, providing expert legal advice on the conviction threshold.
The panel includes retired Chief Justices Artemio V. Panganiban, Reynato S. Puno, and Adolf S. Azcuna, with Hilario G. Davide Jr. submitting a legal memorandum instead of appearing in person.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Four retired Supreme Court (SC) justices will serve as amici curiae or “friends of the court” in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte and weigh in on the 16-vote threshold for conviction.

Senate Impeachment Court spokesperson Reginald Tongol on Thursday, September 10, said the court has secured the formal participation of four retired justices as of 2 pm, with three physically appearing before the impeachment court on Wednesday, September 16.
The three are :

items: Retired Chief Justice Artemio V. Panganiban
Retired Chief Justice Reynato S. Puno
Retired Associate Justice Adolf S. Azcuna

blocks.text: Retired Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide Jr., who served as presiding officer during the impeachment trial of former President Joseph Estrada in 2000, will also participate but will submit a legal memorandum instead of appearing in person.

“The Impeachment Court commends the prompt cooperation of these distinguished jurists. Securing their counsel marks a critical procedural milestone, ensuring that this trial proceeds anchored on verified constitutional bedrock,” said Tongol.

According to Tongol, the four-man panel constitutes the court’s initial list of amici curiae and additional experts may still be invited. He also said the court will not release or comment on any substantive details as regards written advisories submitted beforehand, adding that senator-judges will hold the right of first review of the documents.

“Since an amicus curiae provides expert legal doctrine, not factual evidence and the constitutional right to cross-examine applies only to fact witnesses, not scholars advising the bench, the legal panels will just sit and listen during the whole presentation,” he said.

During the September 16 proceedings, Tongol said the three-member live panel of amici curiae will present their advisories, while Davide’s memorandum will be formally entered into the record. Only senator-judges will be allowed to ask clarificatory questions.

On September 23, the House prosecution panel and Duterte’s defense counsel will each be given exactly 15 minutes for oral arguments on the appeal. After a final round of questions from the senator-judges, the impeachment court will vote on the record, with time allotted for senator-judges to explain their votes.
“The Impeachment Court will not rush the resolution of this constitutional threshold. Doctrinal accuracy and constitutional exactitude take precedence over speed,” said Tongol.

The impeachment court raised discussions on inviting amici curiae after Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo sought clarification on the voting threshold for Duterte’s conviction or acquittal, citing the continued absence of four senators.
Four senator-judges were absent on day 23 of the trial: Loren Legarda, Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, Rodante Marcoleta and Jinggoy Estrada.
Legarda remains under extended medical leave abroad due to lung illness while Dela Rosa is in hiding in view of an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court (ICC).
Marcoleta and Estrada are detained for separate plunder charges.
Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution states that the conviction of an impeachable official requires the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate. – Rappler.com

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Justice (DOJ) is aiming to complete its review of the documents related to the United States’ request to extradite Kingdom of Jesus Christ founder Apollo Quiboloy in the next two weeks.

DOJ Secretary Fredderick Vida said in a press briefing on Thursday, September 10, that the "voluminous" extradition documents are given priority to fulfill the country’s treaty obligations with the US.

“We’re evaluating everything, but definitely we’re giving it the priority it deserves. We have treaty obligations with the United States, we have extradition treaty rules provided by the Supreme Court. Lahat po ito ay dadaan sa tamang proseso,” Vida said.
The Justice Secretary said they hope to complete the evaluation in the next two weeks before filing a petition in court.
“Tinitignan po natin ay matapos po ‘yung evaluation ng Department of Justice within the next two weeks po para maisalang na natin kung ano ang dapat isalang,” he said.
(We are looking to complete the evaluation of the Department of Justice within the next two weeks so we can file what we need to file.)

The US government formally requested Quiboloy’s extradition earlier in August over a 2021 federal indictment in California, where he faces charges of alleged conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, sex trafficking of children, substantive sex trafficking, conspiracy and bulk cash smuggling.
Currently, Quiboloy remains detained as he faces qualified human trafficking and child and sexual abuse cases. He was arrested in September 2024 in Davao City.
The allegations remain pending, and Quiboloy has denied wrongdoing.

articles.title: Grace Tame apologises for comments labelling rape of Israeli women during Hamas attacks ‘propaganda’
articles.summary:
The former Australian of the Year said she stood with survivors of sexual violence ‘everywhere’ and ‘no matter who they are’

  • Get our

blocks.text: Grace Tame has apologised for her comments labelling the rape of Israeli women by Hamas during the 7 October attacks as “propaganda” and “debunked”, saying her words were “misinterpreted”.
The former Australian of the Year issued the apology in an Instagram video on Thursday. The comments were made in an ABC interview about Israel and Gaza in March.
In the video, Tame said she stood with survivors of sexual violence “everywhere, no matter who they are”.
“There’s something I’ve wanted to clarify for a while, which I regret not clarifying sooner. I stand with survivors of sexual violence everywhere, no matter who they are”, she said.

“Comments I made on ABC radio in March this year were misinterpreted to mean that I disbelieve Israeli survivors of sexual violence. This is not the case. I always have, and always will stand with survivors of sexual violence,” she said.
Tame said Human Rights Watch had been unable to find evidence to support the claim that Israeli women were raped en masse on 7 October 2023.
“However, I do not deny the legitimate accusations of rape made by individual Israeli women, including accounts of gang-rape,” she said.
“I do not hate Israelis. I do not hate Jewish people. I abhor the crimes of the State of Israel.

“I believe Israeli survivors, I believe Jewish survivors, as I believe all survivors. While the intention of my remarks was not to imply otherwise, I acknowledge and sincerely apologise for any harm their mischaracterisation has caused.”
Lynda Ben-Menashe, the president of the National Council of Jewish Women Australia, lashed Tame’s statement, saying it was not an apology.

“She called Israeli women’s widely proven claims of sexual violence ‘debunked propaganda,’ which added insult to their injury, and fanned the flames of incitement against all Jewish women – and men in this country,” she said in a statement.
“Saying she’s sorry for how people interpreted her words is not an apology. It neither rehabilitates her nor reverses the damage her original words did to us.”
after newsletter promotion
In the March interview, Tame was asked whether she had expressed outrage about Israeli women who were sexually assaulted during the 7 October attacks.
She said: “I’m not going to sink to the level of entertaining any kind of propaganda” and that “those things have been debunked”.

In 2024, the United Nation’s special envoy on sexual violence in conflict concluded there were “reasonable grounds” to believe sexual assaults including rape and gang-rape in several places took place during the 7 October attacks by Hamas.
Tame’s comments drew a rebuke from the Israeli embassy in Canberra, with a social media post accusing her of losing her “moral compass”.
The ABC’s ombudsman’s office said it received 145 complaints after Tame’s interview, while a further four raised “distinct but similar matters”.

articles.title: Tourists in England face nightly levy on hotel and Airbnb stays under new plans
articles.summary:
Labelled a tourist tax, proposals would give mayors power to decide how revenue raised should be invested

Holidaymakers will face a nightly levy on hotel stays and Airbnb-style visits in…

blocks.text: Holidaymakers will face a nightly levy on hotel stays and Airbnb-style visits in England under plans ministers are due to outline to give mayors new powers.

The idea, labelled a tourist tax, was first raised by Keir Starmer’s government in November and is similar to a scheme running in Scotland. It would allow mayors to charge a fee to visitors staying overnight and decide how the revenue raised should be invested.

The tax could raise hundreds of millions of pounds for mayors to put into transport and public services, but it is likely to be seen as a blow for the hospitality industry, which was squeezed by tax rises and extra employment costs announced in last year’s budget.

The housing secretary, Angela Rayner, is meeting mayors on Thursday, and is expected to outline that the levy will be charged as a percentage of the cost of accommodation, rather than as a flat fee, to protect budget holidays.
Mayors are expected to be given the power to decide what is best for their local area, but ministers do not expect the levy to become overly expensive.

Allen Simpson, the chief executive of UKHospitality, said the plans would put jobs at risk in some communities, and the new tourism tax in Edinburghwas “already having damaging effects”. He told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme holidays in the UK were “already more expensive” than they appeared because of higher VAT.

“What we’re talking about here is an open-ended power for mayors to set tourism taxes at any level they want,” said Simpson. “And remember that if you go to Paris, if you go to Rome, if you go to Berlin, you’re paying a small tourism tax, but it’s capped.”

He added: “It will be the case that you’ll have holiday parks which can’t open in the shoulder seasons and of course people who go on holiday will just have that little bit less money in their pocket.”

The overnight visitor levy was outlined in the king’s speech in May, but legislation was not brought forward before Starmer was ousted as prime minister. Andy Burnham is likely to pitch the policy as part of his wider devolution agenda. No 10 has previously said local leaders would be “able to set out plans for how revenues will be invested by March 2028”.

As mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham introduced the city visitor charge in April 2023 – a £1 per room per night fee – to pay for measures aimed at attracting more visitors. Last year other mayors, including Sadiq Khan in London, wrote a letter to the culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, and Reeves urging the government to introduce a visitor levy.
after newsletter promotion

Edinburgh became the first city in Scotland to introduce a tourist tax at 5% in July after the Scottish parliament passed a law last year granting councils the power to implement their own visitor levies. In Wales, councils will have the power to charge £1.30 a person a night in tax for most accommodation from April 2027.

But UKHospitality, which represents thousands of restaurants, hotels and pubs, has said a tourism tax of 5% would be one of the highest tourist tax rates in Europe. It has written to Burnham urging him to consider plans for a “holiday bonus” instead, as households continue to struggle with the cost of living.
Tourist taxes are common in Europe and the rest of the world, and are used in cities such as New York, Barcelona and Venice to fund local services.

articles.title: Search expands after Palawan ferry fire kills 5 and leaves dozens missing
articles.summary: Authorities estimate that more than 80 people remain unaccounted for, although the figures could still change

blocks.text: FIRE. MV June Aster burns as flames and smoke rise after a fire broke out on the ferry, off the coast of Palawan, Philippines, in this screengrab taken from a handout video released on September 9, 2026.
Philippine Coast Guard/Handout via REUTERS
Authorities estimate that more than 80 people remain unaccounted for, although the figures could still change

items: A search and rescue operation is ongoing off Palawan after a passenger ferry caught fire, resulting in five fatalities and many missing.
The Philippine Coast Guard has deployed multiple vessels and is using drift-modelling tools to locate survivors, with 43 people rescued so far.
The ferry, which had 117 passengers and 17 crew members, is under investigation for the cause of the fire, amidst concerns about safety regulations in the country's maritime travel.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – A large-scale search and rescue operation was underway off the western Philippine island of Palawan on Thursday, September 10, after a passenger ferry caught fire, killing five people and leaving dozens of passengers missing.

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said multiple vessels and other assets were deployed to search for survivors, while rescue teams were using drift-modelling tools to identify areas where people may have been carried by currents.

Based on the vessel’s manifest, the number of survivors, currently at 43, and the fatalities reported so far, authorities estimated that more than 80 people remained unaccounted for, although the figures could still change.

Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said rescuers could not yet enter the vessel, with the search hampered by thick smoke still billowing from the ferry as well as concerns about extreme heat and the risk of explosions.
Drone footage released by the Coast Guard showed the blackened ferry surrounded by clear blue-green waters, with the vessel still generating smoke hours after the fire broke out on Wednesday night.

Cayabyab said the vessel’s manifest listed a total of 117 passengers and 17 crew members. The ferry had departed from Baseco in Manila and was bound for Coron, a popular tourist destination in Palawan known for its diving sites, beaches and island-hopping attractions.

Among the 43 people rescued were two Chilean nationals, said Aileen Ausente, spokesperson for PCG in Palawan, adding that air assets were on standby to help with rescue operations, the weather permitting.
The burned ferry had drifted farther from its original location overnight, carried by currents and winds, adding to the challenges facing rescuers, Cayabyab said.
The cause of the fire is under investigation.
Ferry travel is a common mode of transport in the Philippines, an archipelago of more than 7,600 islands, where millions of people rely on boats to travel between provinces.
The country has a patchy maritime safety record, and many previous ferry disasters have been linked to overcrowding, rough weather and lax enforcement of safety regulations. – Rappler.com

articles.title: China hits back at Teodoro after he rejects note on South China Sea
articles.summary: China told Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. to stop his "provocations and theatrics" after he publicly rebuked Beijing's position on the South China Sea arbitration in Seoul, South Korea.

blocks.text: September 10, 2026 | 4:09pm
Combination photo shows Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa and Pedro Pardo

MANILA, Philippines — China told Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. to stop his "provocations and theatrics" after he publicly rebuked Beijing's position on the South China Sea arbitration in Seoul, South Korea.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Wednesday, September 9, that she was not familiar with the incident but reiterated China's rejection of the 2016 arbitral ruling.
"China’s position has always been clear on the so-called 'South China Sea arbitration,'" Mao said in a statement posted on the Facebook page of the Chinese Embassy in the Philippines.
She said the Philippines "unilaterally initiated the case," calling it a "distortion and abuse" of the dispute settlement mechanism under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
"It is the Philippine side who has violated UNCLOS and undermined its integrity and authority," Mao said.
"We urge the certain individual of the Philippine side to cut the provocations and theatrics, and stop undermining China-Philippines relations and stability in the South China Sea," she added.
'Of course, because you lost'
Mao's remarks came a day after Teodoro received a handwritten note from a Chinese official while answering a question on the South China Sea at the Seoul Defense Dialogue.
The note came from the office of the Chinese embassy's defense attaché in Seoul, who was attending the forum, the Korea JoongAng Daily reported, citing multiple sources.
The Seoul Defense Dialogue is hosted by South Korea's defense ministry and is among the region's larger annual gatherings of defense officials.
The note reiterated China's rejection of the 2016 ruling, saying the arbitration was "illegal, null and void."
Teodoro read portions of the note onstage and responded to each point.
When the note said China "neither accepted nor recognized" the ruling, Teodoro replied: "Of course, because you lost."
Teodoro also questioned why the note was handed to him while he was speaking at the forum.
"How can you deal with a country in an international forum, beyond the question asked to me, disrespecting the organizers of this forum, how do you expect to deal with it civilly?" he said.
China rejects ruling

The Philippines brought its case against China before an arbitral tribunal under UNCLOS in 2013. The tribunal ruled in 2016 that China had no legal basis to claim historic rights to resources within areas covered by the Philippines' exclusive economic zone.
China has consistently rejected the ruling, saying it is "illegal, null and void" and has no binding force.
The latest exchange comes amid continuing tensions between Manila and Beijing over the South China Sea.

China sanctioned Teodoro and his family in June, barring them from entering mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau and prohibiting Chinese organizations and individuals from conducting transactions with them. — with a report from Cristina Chi

articles.title: Ecuador: Ex-president Bucaram sentenced in corruption case
articles.summary: Abdala Bucaram, Ecuador's former president, was convicted of organized crime for his role in the illegal sale of COVID-19 tests and medical supplies, receiving a prison sentence of over nine years.

image.caption: Abdala Bucaram received the sentence while at a guarded clinicImage: Jose Sanchez Lindao/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Abdala Bucaram, Ecuador's former president, was found guilty of corruption and sentenced on Wednesday to nine years and four months in prison for being "collaborators" in organized crime.
Bucaram's son, Jacob Bucaram, was also sentenced for the illegal sale of at least21,000 COVID-19 tests and other medical supplies during the pandemic in 2020.
The trial, which lasted six years, continued following an appeal from the attorney general's office, after a judge dismissed the charges against Bucaram and his son in 2021.
What are the details of the case?
Bucaram heard the decision remotely from a guarded clinic in Guayaquil where he was receiving medical care
He was arrested in 2020 following a raid on his home in Guayaquil, and was put under house arrest as he could not initially be imprisoned due to health problems.
The former president has undergone surgery for heart issues and was admitted to intensive care.
Bucaram posted a message on X stating that he had requested to be discharged from the clinic "despite being at risk of sudden death."
"I will be able to defend myself, and the country will learn horrifying things about this process," he added.
According to the investigation,COVID-19 tests were illegally transferred to Bucaram's residence, which was guarded by Quito traffic agents.
According to the public prosecutor's office, the tests and medical supplies were sold in various provinces of the country "without invoices and without paying taxes to the state."
Bucaram was removed from office in 1997 after being declared mentally unfit to rule, and had lived in exile in Panama for nearly two decades before returning to Ecuador in 2017.
