articles.title: Philippine Science High School campus proposed for Albay
articles.summary: LEGAZPI CITY — An Albay campus of the Philippine Science High School (PSHS) has been included in the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program with an initial allocation of P100 million, according…

blocks.text: LEGAZPI CITY — An Albay campus of the Philippine Science High School (PSHS) has been included in the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program with an initial allocation of P100 million, according to Albay Third District Rep. Raymond Adrian Salceda in an interview on Tuesday (September 8).
The campus would rise on a site at Barangay Itaran in Polangui town and is expected to help address the demand for specialized science and technology education in the province, Salceda said.
“If the project pushes through, it would serve not only students from Albay but also those from nearby provinces in the Bicol region,” he said.
Salceda said he presented the proposal to the PSHS Board of Trustees, which expressed support for the project, along with the administration of the PSHS-Bicol Regional Campus in Goa, Camarines Sur.
The first phase of the project is estimated to cost about P300 million and will cover the construction of academic and administrative buildings, site development, roads and utility infrastructure.
Members of the PSHS board conducted an ocular inspection of the proposed site on Monday (September 7) and gave a positive feedback, Salceda said.

He said his office had also sought assistance from the Department of Public Works and Highways and the Department of Science and Technology to secure additional funding and enable the campus to admit its first batch of students by 2029.
“Albay produces the highest number of qualifiers in the annual PSHS admission examination, but many are unable to continue because the Goa campus is too far,” Salceda said.
“We hope this new campus will make the dream of becoming scientists more accessible to many Albayanos,” he added. INQ

articles.title: Habagat, trough of TD to drench Luzon, Visayas Wednesday
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The southwest monsoon or habagat and the trough of a tropical depression outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) will bring rains over Luzon and parts of the Visayas…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The southwest monsoon or habagat and the trough of a tropical depression outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) will bring rains over Luzon and parts of the Visayas on Wednesday, the state weather bureau said.

According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), occasional rains will persist over Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro.
Because of the habagat, cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms are also expected in Metro Manila, the rest of Luzon, Aklan, and Antique.
Moreover, the Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley and Aurora may experience cloudy skies with scattered rains due to the trough of the tropical depression.
“Ito ‘yung dati nating binantayan na si Pilandok na may international name na Krovan,” weather specialist Chenel Dominguez said in Pagasa’s morning weather briefing.
(This is the same system we previously monitored as Pilandok, with the international name Krovan.)
“Umaabot ‘yung extension ng kaulapan neto dito sa may Northern Luzon na ito rin ang nagdadala ng mga pag-ulan dito sa lugar na ito,” she added.
(Its cloudiness extends over Northern Luzon, which is also bringing rains to the area.)
Meanwhile, in Mindanao and the rest of Visayas, hot and humid weather is likely to persist.
No low-pressure area (LPA) is being monitored by Pagasa within PAR this Wednesday. However, the formation of an LPA is not being ruled out by the bureau.
“By Friday, September 11, inaasahan natin, may posibilidad tayong mabuo na low pressure area na magpapalakas dito sa ating habagat,” Dominguez said.
(By Friday, September 11, we expect that a low-pressure area may form, which could strengthen the habagat.) /jpv

articles.title: Singapore boosts PM’s salary by $1m amid major pay rise for ministers
articles.summary:
The affluent city-state has justified high-end salaries for its political leaders, arguing they attract talent and ensure good governance

Singapore’s prime minister has been given a $1m pay…

blocks.text: Singapore’s prime minister has been given a $1m pay rise as the affluent city-state announced a dramatic one-off salary boost for government ministers.
The pay increases add more than 60% to what are already the world’s highest ministerial salaries.

Singapore has justified high-end salaries for its political leaders, arguing they attract talent and ensure good governance. The issue is nevertheless politically sensitive, with cabinet members’ income far exceeding that of most ordinary citizens.
Prime minister Lawrence Wong’s benchmark annual salary will rise from S$2.2m ($1.7m) to S$3.6m ($2.8m).
The deputy prime minister’s benchmark will lift from S$1.8m to S$3m. Cabinet ministers will get between S$1.8m and S$2.8m, depending on the seniority and weight of their portfolio.
Wong said he would donate the entire increase of his salary to “suitable good causes” during his term.

Even before the raise, the Singaporean prime minister’s paycheck vastly outstripped the wages of many other leaders, including in the US and other G7 nations. The US president earns $400,000 a year, while the UK prime minister is paid about $230,000 annually.

“Political salaries are a difficult and emotive issue,” said Wong, whose long-ruling People’s Action Party dominates Singapore’s parliament and its 21-member cabinet. “The sums involved are more than what most citizens earn, so I understand why Singaporeans scrutinise them closely, and why many feel strongly about the matter.”
However, the issue is “ultimately about whether Singapore will continue to have the quality of political leadership we need to take our country forward” in the decades ahead, he said.
“Our starting point is this: good government depends on good leadership.”
The South-east Asian nation, which last adjusted ministerial salaries 15 years ago, is regularly ranked among the world’s least corrupt countries.
Wong said the pay raises were recommended by an independent committee, adding that existing office holders would not be moved immediately to the new benchmarks.
They will receive a one-off adjustment of up to 9% from 15 October, depending on individual circumstances, including performance.

articles.title: US bans Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles as trade war escalates
articles.summary:
Trump responds after Canada imposes $20bn in retaliatory tariffs and Canadian PM vows to diversify trade abroad

The US is banning dairy products, most alcoholic beverages and motorcycles…

blocks.text: The US is banning dairy products, most alcoholic beverages and motorcycles from Canada, the White House said on Tuesday, as the trade war between the two neighbors and longtime allies escalates.
The ban will take effect in three weeks and comes after Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on $20bn in US imports earlier on Tuesday.

Donald Trump also moved to shut Canadian products out of large, long-term US government contracts as Canada’s retaliatory tariffs took effect and the prime minister, Mark Carney, vowed to speed efforts to reduce the country’s dependence on the United States.
The US president directed the General Services Administration to declare Canadian products ineligible for those contracts until Canada allows “full and fair reciprocity″ for American products.
Carney said on Tuesday that Canada’s strategy was about becoming more independent. “It’s about ensuring that no country can hold us hostage. And that we can live how we want to live.”

The rupture has upended one of the world’s closest relationships. On 22 August, the US imposed 50% tariffs on about 5% of Canadian imports, charging that Canada had unfairly treated the American dairy, alcoholic beverage and auto industries.

The US and Canada have long sparred over trade, particularly Canada’s protected dairy market and the US government’s allegations that it subsidizes producers of softwood lumber. But they remained friends and staunch allies.

Under Trump, US-Canada relations have deteriorated rapidly. In addition to imposing tariffs on Canadian products, Trump has repeatedly made inflammatory comments about making Canada the 51st US state. Carney came to power in a come-from-behind political victory last year by promising to stand up to him.
Some Canadian provinces have banned the sale of US alcoholic products – a move that prompted the retaliatory US ban on Tuesday.
How the trade war ends could carry consequences far beyond Canada, testing whether a smaller US ally can resist Trump’s economic pressure without being forced to yield.

Earlier on Tuesday, a Canadian official said Ottawa did not intend to change course regardless of whether Trump responded with nothing or what the official called a “nuclear response”. The government’s strategy will remain focused on building more at home and diversifying trade abroad, the official said.

The tariffs hit hundreds of American products, including steel, aluminum, cheese, appliances, clothing, cosmetics and farm equipment, at rates of 15%, 25% or 50%. They cover about $20bn in American goods, roughly 6% of the $333.6bn the United States exported to Canada last year.
Since Canada-US trade talks collapsed 21 August, Trump and his administration have imposed additional tariffs and issued a series of threats and attacks portraying Canada as weak and dependent.

Trump’s trade war and repeated talk of making Canada the 51st state have fueled anger across the country. Canadians have sharply cut travel to the United States and boycotted US goods, moves Carney praised as signs of national resolve.
Gabriel Brunet, a spokesperson for Canada-US trade minister Dominic LeBlanc, said officials from both countries remain in contact even though formal talks have not resumed.

articles.title: Police maintain perimeter security as Romualdez remains hospitalized
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Police personnel continue to provide perimeter security outside Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City amid the ongoing confinement of former House Speaker Martin…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Police personnel continue to provide perimeter security outside Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City amid the ongoing confinement of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, who is reportedly being treated for various ailments.
Romualdez, who was arrested Monday over a P7.4-billion plunder case, is currently under the custody of the Philippine National Police (PNP) while confined at the medical center.

Police deployed outside the medical center as of 6 a.m. on Wednesday told the INQUIRER that they are on a shifting schedule to maintain 24/7 security while the former House speaker remains at the hospital.
Another unit of PNP personnel was deployed inside the medical center’s lobby.
On Tuesday, San Juan police chief Col. Anthony Gantang conducted an inspection of their deployment in and around the hospital.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla earlier said they will request the Sandiganbayan to transfer Romualdez to the PNP General Hospital at Camp Crame in Quezon City.
Remulla announced this as he said that the former speaker had suffered a stroke and a transient ischemic attack—or the temporary blockage of blood to part of the brain—last July.

On Monday, the Sandiganbayan Third Division issued an arrest warrant against Romualdez, former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co, and two others, hours after the Office of the Ombudsman filed the nonbailable plunder case.
The charges stemmed from allegations that they received around P7.4 billion in kickbacks from government projects between 2022 and 2025.
The former House speaker was arrested at the medical center hours after the arrest warrant issuance on Monday, while his three co-accused remain at large. /jpv

articles.title: Brahminy kite rescued in Tayabas City
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — A Brahminy kite (Haliastur indus), locally known as “lawin,” was found at a business establishment in Tayabas City, Quezon, on Monday (Sept. 7). The City Environment and Natural…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — A Brahminy kite (Haliastur indus), locally known as “lawin,” was found at a business establishment in Tayabas City, Quezon, on Monday (Sept. 7).

The City Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) said in a report that the medium-sized bird of prey was immediately turned over to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources for proper care and disposition.

The Brahminy kite is a raptor commonly found in coastal and lowland areas. As both a predator and scavenger, it plays an important role in maintaining ecological balance by feeding on small animals and carrion, according to wildlife literature.
CENRO reminded the public that hunting, collecting, or possessing wildlife is prohibited and punishable under Republic Act No. 9147, or the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001.
“Report any form of abuse or illegal activity that may harm our environment and natural resources,” the office said. /jpv

articles.title: PNP reports P3.4-M haul from La Union drug busts in a week
articles.summary: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union – The Ilocos Regional Police’s campaign against illegal drugs led to the confiscation of P3.4 million worth of suspected shabu and marijuana plants, during crime…

blocks.text: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union – The Ilocos Regional Police’s campaign against illegal drugs led to the confiscation of P3.4 million worth of suspected shabu and marijuana plants, during crime suppression operations conducted from September 1-7.

A police report showed that it conducted 25 operations during which they arrested 24 suspects in possession of 411.48 grams of suspected shabu, 2,740 fully grown marijuana plants, 1,400 marijuana seedlings, and 30 grams of dried marijuana leaves.
The intensified manhunt operations also secured the arrest of 56 fugitives, including seven most wanted persons (MWPs) and 49 other wanted suspects, the report said.
The police’s 20 operations against illegal gambling also led to the arrest of 20 suspects and the confiscation of bet money amounting to P33,457.00.
The drive against loose firearms likewise accounted for nine weapons, consisting of six surrendered and three deposited firearms.

“Our weekly accomplishments reflect the police’s commitment to responsive and effective law enforcement. We will remain relentless in our operations and steadfast in safeguarding the peace, safety, and security of communities across the Ilocos Region,” said Brig. Gen. Crisaleo Tolentino, Ilocos police director, in a statement.
The Ilocos Region is composed of the provinces of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union and Pangasinan. /jpv

articles.title: Two held, P3.5-M worth of fuel seized in Marinduque
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Two suspects were arrested and around P3.54 million worth of petroleum products and transport equipment were seized in a joint police operation in Gasan, Marinduque,…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Two suspects were arrested and around P3.54 million worth of petroleum products and transport equipment were seized in a joint police operation in Gasan, Marinduque, on Tuesday (Sept. 8).

The suspects were arrested in Barangay Bachao Ibaba after they were caught distributing and dispensing petroleum products using a tanker allegedly without the required Department of Energy (DOE) authority and permit, according to the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) and the MIMAROPA police.

Seized during the operation were about 19,800 liters of petroleum products valued at P1.734 million, consisting of 12,000 liters of premium gasoline, 6,000 liters of diesel and 1,800 liters of unleaded gasoline.

Police also confiscated a blue-and-white 10-wheeler tank lorry valued at about P1.805 million, a black suction hose, the vehicle’s official receipt and certificate of registration, and a delivery receipt.
The total estimated value of the seized petroleum products and equipment was placed at P3.538 million.

The suspects would.be charged for violating Section 2 (a), in relation to Section 3 (h), of Batas Pambansa Blg. 33, as amended by Presidential Decree No. 1865, which penalizes unlawful acts involving petroleum products. /jpv

articles.title: Mindoro missionary, teacher Fr. Edgar Javier dies at 77
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro – Divine Word missionary and scholar Fr. Edgar Javier, SVD, who served the Church for five decades, mostly in Mindoro, had passed away on Tuesday (Sept. 8). He was 77.…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro – Divine Word missionary and scholar Fr. Edgar Javier, SVD, who served the Church for five decades, mostly in Mindoro, had passed away on Tuesday (Sept. 8). He was 77.
Javier died at around 10 a.m., according to the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of the Philippines (CBCP) News.

The Society of the Divine Word (SVD) did not disclose the cause of his death. “We entrust him to God’s loving embrace and give thanks for his life of service, compassion, and missionary zeal,” the SVD said.
Javier’s missionary journey took him from Mindoro to the Pacific and later to the Philippines’ seminaries and theological institutions, where he helped form priests, religious and missionaries.
For Catholic communities in Mindoro, he is particularly remembered for his early missionary service in Occidental Mindoro and ministry among the Mangyan communities.
Born on May 5, 1949 in Guimba town, Nueva Ecija, Javier entered the Christ the King Mission Seminary in 1968 and was ordained a priest on Sept. 5, 1975.
He began his missionary ministry in Mindoro, serving at St. Augustine Parish and the St. Joseph Parish Mangyan Mission in San Jose town, Occidental Mindoro, from 1976 to 1979.
He later served as chancellor of the Apostolic Vicariate of Calapan, which is now the Diocese of Calapan.
Javier pursued advanced studies in missiology at the Pontifical Gregorian University in Rome, earning a licentiate in 1982 and a doctorate in 1985.
He served as a missionary in Samoa from 1985 to 1995 and Fiji from 1995 to 1999 before returning to the Philippines, where he focused on priestly formation, missiological education and research.

He taught at Christ the King Mission Seminary and headed the Mission Institute in Tagaytay before becoming director of the Divine Word Institute of Mission Studies (DWIMS). He also taught at several theological institutions in the Philippines and served as a visiting professor in Vietnam and Macau.
For his former co-faculty at DWIMS, Fr. Andy Peter Lubi, Javier was more than an academic.
“Fr. Egay Javier is an intimately engaging person and a deeply passionate mentor, one who challenges and brings out the best in his students,” Lubi said.
Fr. Renz Hernandez, one of Javier’s students in missiology, said Javier encouraged him to pursue a master’s degree in the field and volunteered to become his thesis adviser.

“As a professor, his way of teaching is engaging and his missiological ideas are profound yet practical. As an adviser, he’s very encouraging and supportive. He reads, checks, and corrects my paper thoroughly,” Hernandez said.
“I will never forget his writing techniques which he imparted to us—the SJA Method (See, Judge, Act) and the RRR Method (Reality, Reflection, Response),” he added.
Javier had marked his 50th year as a priest in 2025. /jpv

articles.title: Teodoro calls out China’s ‘disrespectful’ note at Seoul forum
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro Jr. on Tuesday described China’s latest assertion, written in a letter regarding the South China Sea arbitration, as “actual coercion,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro Jr. on Tuesday described China’s latest assertion, written in a letter regarding the South China Sea arbitration, as “actual coercion, bullying and aggression”.
His denunciation came after a man handed him, on stage, a piece of paper during a question-and-answer session at the Seoul Defense Dialogue, an annual multilateral security forum.

“China’s position on the South China Sea arbitration is clear, consistent, and firm. They have no position. The arbitration violates fundamental principles of international law,” the letter stated as read aloud by Teodoro.
The defense chief slammed China’s assertion, saying that they only refused to recognize the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (Unclos) after losing the arbitral tribunal.
The Unclos 2016 ruling is a landmark award that recognizes the Philippines’ claim over the West Philippine Sea.
Teodoro, moreover, said that the move was a blatant disrespect to the international forum, particularly to the Republic of Korea,.

“It not only disrespects, shows, if this is a Chinese position said to me, it not only disrespects international law, throwing Unclos to the floor and trampling upon it, but it also disrespects the basic decency that should be accorded to our most gracious hosts, the Republic of Korea and the rest of the audience here,” he expressed.
He added that China should observe “basic decency.”
Teodoro said in a video posted on Facebook that the man who delivered the letter to him was a Chinese delegate.
The defense chief earlier spoke at the first plenary session attended by international defense leaders, where he pushed for a collaborative security architecture across Asia. /cb

articles.title: Judges speak out after peer got trolled by Sara Duterte diehards
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — An organization of trial court judges reminded the public that judges should be able to perform their duty without fear, after one of them became the subject of online…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — An organization of trial court judges reminded the public that judges should be able to perform their duty without fear, after one of them became the subject of online harassment for issuing an arrest warrant last week against Vice President Sara Duterte.

The Kapunungan sa mga Pilipinong Hukom (Hukom), a group of first- and second-level trial court judges from various provinces, expressed grave concern over the “unfounded accusations” against Judge Maria Angelica de Ramos of Quezon City Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 98, which will hear the grave threats case against the Vice President.

Since the warrant came out on Sept. 4, social media posts mainly by Duterte’s supporters have shared background information on De Ramos, insinuating bias because she was appointed to the post last year by President Marcos.
Some included her photo, with the caption: “Remember the face!”

Duterte on Saturday posted a bail at P360,000 for the charges arising from her online press briefing in November 2024, where she said she had talked to someone to have President Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and former Speaker Martin Romualdez killed if an alleged murder plot against her succeeded.
Before the procedure, the Vice President was heard telling her lawyers that she was fearing for her life and she didn’t trust the court, the police or even her own security personnel.

“While freedom to criticize the courts and judicial decisions is vital in a democracy, vilification of judges undermines judicial independence and public confidence in the rule of law,” Hukom said in a statement on Tuesday.
“Judges must decide cases freely, according to law, without fear or pressure—even when rulings are unpopular,” it stressed.

Hukom reminded netizens that social media is “not a courtroom” and that “digital mobs are not justice,” stressing that government officials, including the Vice President, should “stand equal before the courts.”

In a phone interview, Hukom president Rosario Caise said the harassment of judges, either through cyberbullying or Red-tagging, are not just an attack on the person but also on the judiciary as an institution.
“Whatever is presented before the courts, that’s our only basis for our decision… Attacking the judge is likewise attacking the institution,” she told the Inquirer.
Formed in 2018, Hukom had come to the defense of other judges who were vilified online because of their rulings.

They include Judge Marlo Malagar of Manila RTC over his dismissal of a petition to declare the Communist Party of the Philippines and its armed wing New People’s Army as “terrorists”; and Judge Monique Quisumbing-Ignacio of Muntinlupa RTC for dismissing the case against journalists Lady Ann Salem and labor organizer Rodrigo Esparago. /cb

articles.title: July unemployment leaps to 6 percent; highest in postpandemic era
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The country’s labor market showed fresh signs of strain in July as more fresh graduates struggled to find jobs, pushing unemployment to its highest level since the pandemic era.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The country’s labor market showed fresh signs of strain in July as more fresh graduates struggled to find jobs, pushing unemployment to its highest level since the pandemic era.

According to data by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) released on Tuesday, the unemployment rate surged to 6 percent in July from 4.9 percent in June. This was equivalent to 3.14 million jobless Filipinos, up from 2.59 million in June.
The latest figure marked the third straight month of increase and was the highest in four years, or since June 2022, when unemployment also stood at 6 percent.
This was also the first time unemployment reached the 6-percent level after staying between 4.7 percent and 5.8 percent since the start of the year.

Month-on-month, the labor force participation rate declined to 63.6 percent from 65.1 percent, translating to a labor force of 52.36 million from 53.25 million. But quarter-on-quarter, it increased from 62.7 percent, or 51.3 million.
Metro Manila had the highest unemployment rate at 8.2 percent.

National Statistician Claire Dennis Mapa said the sudden rise in unemployment was due to new participants estimated at 1.33 million who have joined the labor market but are not yet absorbed into the workforce.
The age group of these entrants was pegged at 15 to 24 years old.
The employment rate declined one percentage point in July from 95 percent in June, with the number of employed Filipinos falling to 49.21 million from 50.55 million.
The number of underemployed Filipinos, meanwhile, rose to 12.9 percent from 12.1 percent. This represented 6.33 million underemployed Filipinos, up from 6.11 million in June.
Quality jobs needed
The Department of Economy, Planning and Development (DepDev) said the spike in unemployment is a challenge.

“More Filipinos are participating in the labor market, which means that we need to intensify efforts to attract investments, especially those that create quality jobs,” DepDev Secretary Arsenio Balisacan said.
“The key is to continuously improve the ease of doing business in the country,” he said.

Economist Leonardo Lanzona of the Ateneo de Manila University said the increase in unemployment is no longer a short-term absorption lag, especially since it had been climbing steadily as the share of degree holders among the jobless rose from 26.9 percent in 2020 to the latest figure of 35.6 percent.

“If this were a short-run absorption lag, it would have been corrected already. We have a structural demographic mismanagement problem which means investment incentives are designed to reward capital size rather than job creation,” Lanzona said.

“The economy keeps attracting capital-intensive investment that can’t absorb a growing young workforce—a design flaw no amount of job-matching or reskilling programs can fix without reforming the incentive criteria themselves,” he added. /cb

articles.title: DILG chief: ‘We won’t allow’ Romualdez to stay at private hospital
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Secretary Jonvic Remulla of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said the agency would ask the Sandiganbayan to have former Speaker Martin Romualdez…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Secretary Jonvic Remulla of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said the agency would ask the Sandiganbayan to have former Speaker Martin Romualdez transferred, as a person under arrest, from a private hospital to the police medical facility inside Camp Crame.
Remulla announced the plan as the antigraft court ordered Romualdez to appear on Thursday regarding his motion seeking continued hospital confinement following his arrest for plunder on Monday night.

The Leyte congressman, a cousin of President Marcos, was served an arrest warrant and underwent police booking procedures at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City, where he had been admitted for anxiety attacks and what Remulla called a “cardiovascular event” hours before the warrant came out.

A motion to have the lawmaker moved to the Philippine National Police General Hospital at Camp Crame, Quezon City, will be filed on Wednesday “just to show you that we won’t allow him to stay at Cardinal Santos,’’ Remulla said.

“We can monitor his condition at Crame, but it’s up to the discretion of the court if he’ll be allowed to be moved to Crame,” he added. “We will give his doctors visitation and practicing rights so they can go to Camp Crame.”

Romualdez, former Ako Bicol Rep. Elizaldy Co and two others were charged with plunder, a nonbailable offense, before the Sandiganbayan over allegations they received more than P7 billion in kickbacks from government projects between 2022 and 2025.

Based on charges prepared by the Office of the Ombudsman, Romualdez and Co were accused of “repeatedly receiving, directly or indirectly, on at least fifteen (15) occasions, commissions, shares, percentages, kickbacks, ‘commitments’ and/or other pecuniary benefits” worth at least P7.44 billion.

The amount allegedly came from contractors, persons and entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and/or other government projects that were funded under the General Appropriations Acts for fiscal years 2022 to 2025.
The P7.44 billion, according to the case, was “specifically traced and laundered [by] setting up and/or using shell or dummy corporations and conduits.”
Respecting legal process
Aside from Romualdez and Co, also named in the charge sheet were a member of the former Speaker’s staff, Jocelyn Sereño, and a certain Felicito Guevarra, the president of a money changer corporation.
In a statement on Monday, Romualdez’s lawyer and spokesperson Ade Fajardo said his client respects the courts and legal process and will face the charges.

“We recognize the public interest surrounding this case. But ultimately, criminal liability must be determined by the evidence presented in court, under the rules and safeguards of our justice system,” Fajardo said.
He said Romualdez was not asking for special treatment but “asks only for the same due process and fair hearing guaranteed to every Filipino.”
Custody
The Sandiganbayan Third Division, in its order on Tuesday, stressed that the court now has custody of Romualdez.

“If there are concerns regarding the accused’s medical condition, it is only this court that can determine whether such condition affects the implementation of the warrant, the confinement of the accused at a hospital, or his commitment to a jail facility,” the court said.
It also issued a subpoena to Romualdez’s doctors Rody Sy, Rogelio Libarres, Kurt Allen Sibayan and Rosalio Torres, ordering their appearance on Thursday.
According to his motion requesting continued hospital stay, Romualdez is suffering from Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, primary hypothyroidism and other illnesses.
According to Remulla, Romualdez suffered a stroke and a transient ischemic attack, or the temporary blockage of blood to a part of the brain, in July.
“It wasn’t that serious. From what I saw, he had no deficiency, but he suffered a cerebrovascular event,” he said.

Regarding security arrangements, Remulla said “We have two armed guards stationed outside his room 24/7. We also have armed guards in the lobby, and a mobile patrol unit waiting outside the hospital.”
Remulla described Romualdez as a “flight risk,” noting that he has “two private jets… three helicopters … and three yachts.”
The DILG on Tuesday also released Romualdez’s official mug shot taken during the booking procedure.
The photo, flashed on screen during a press briefing in Camp Crame, shows Romualdez in a hospital bed with an orange PNP detainee shirt placed on top of his medical gown.
No instruction
The PNP earlier explained that Romualdez could not be made to stand up for the photo or wear the orange shirt due to the medical implements attached to his body.
Remulla maintained he had not received any instruction from President Marcos on how to treat the former House leader.

“The President has no male sibling, so Romualdez is his closest cousin. If you think this was easy for him, it wasn’t,” Remulla said. “If you’re asking whether there were instructions on how to treat him, there was none. Zero.”
Remulla also told reporters that he and Romualdez briefly spoke during the serving of the warrant, noting that they were fraternity brothers at the University of the Philippines.

“He had no requests… I told him, ‘Brother, I hope you understand why I am doing this. It’s nothing personal.’ And he said, ‘It’s okay, I understand.’ That was the entire length of our conversation,” he said.

Reacting to criticism over Romualdez happening to be at a hospital just hours before the warrant was released, the interior secretary said: “That’s the hard part. We do not have the right to intercept (an accused) before the warrant of arrest is issued by the court.”

“They (the accused and his lawyers) knew the charges were filed. They knew the case was raffled, so they got ahead of it. In this case, actually, it’s only with Speaker Martin that that’s happened … I don’t believe in coincidences, so we take it at that,” he said. /cb

articles.title: PH improves rank in int’l education assessment
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Three years after ranking near the bottom of international learning assessments in 2022, the Philippines expanded its reach in 2025, surpassing 18 education systems in reading,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Three years after ranking near the bottom of international learning assessments in 2022, the Philippines expanded its reach in 2025, surpassing 18 education systems in reading, 16 in mathematics, and 14 in science.
Based on the latest Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) results, the Philippines, when ranked from the bottom, placed 15th in science, 17th in mathematics, and 19th in reading.
In the 2022 PISA results, the Philippines ranked sixth from the bottom in reading and mathematics and third from the bottom in science, out of 81 participating countries.
In response to the 2022 performance, the advocacy group Philippine Business for Education warned that the country’s education system was in its “worst state”.

This year, the Philippines obtained a mean score of 373 in science, 371 in mathematics, and 367 in reading, representing increases of 17, 16, and 20 points, respectively, from the country’s 2022 Pisa results.

Data from OECD also showed that the Philippines is among the countries showing big changes between 2022 and 2025, with Georgia, Cambodia, Jordan, Montenegro, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Thailand, and Turkiye on top of the list.

The assessment, conducted by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), aims to evaluate the academic performance of more than 760,000 students aged 15 across partner countries every three years.
Highest score since joining

Education Secretary Sonny Angara on Tuesday announced the marked improvement in the Philippines’ performance, with Filipino students achieving their highest Pisa scores to date in reading, mathematics, and science.

Angara presented the results during the national launch at Caloocan City Science High School, highlighting gains across all three subject areas as he cited the Marcos administration’s continuing efforts to improve the country’s learning outcomes.
“This is a significant achievement for our learners and for the entire Philippine education system,” Angara said.

“But more than the numbers, we are seeing evidence that our learners are capable of making real and meaningful progress,” he added. “We should be proud of how far our learners and teachers have come, but we should be even more determined about how much farther we can go.”

Andreas Schleicher, OECD Director for Education and Skills, congratulated Filipino teachers and school leaders for the results, saying “what you have achieved in this latest round of OECD’s Pisa assessment is not just good news for the Philippines, it’s a story that deserves to be noticed far beyond your borders.”
The latest results show that the share of Filipino learners attaining Level 2 or higher, which is the baseline proficiency level under Pisa, has increased.
In science, the proportion rose from 23 percent to 32 percent; in mathematics, from 16 percent to 21 percent; and in reading, from 24 percent to 31 percent.
Bullying scores
However, Angara also noted that the Philippines recorded an increase in verbal and cyber bullying in schools compared to the 2022 Pisa results.
Based on the 2025 data, 33 percent of students claimed that other students made fun of them compared to the 22 percent reported in 2022.
Reports on the spread of rumors across students also increased from 15 percent to 19 percent in the latest assessment.
Reported experiences of physical bullying among Filipino students reflected only a one-percentage-point decrease from last year’s results, changing from 16 percent to 15 percent.
Meanwhile, reported threats between students remained at 19 percent in both the 2022 and 2025 Pisa results.
‘On the right track’
In a statement, the Second Congressional Commission on Education (Edcom 2) hailed the latest Pisa results and said the country’s educational reforms were “on the right track” and “gaining momentum.”

“This progress belongs to the entire country,” the commission said, noting that “over the past three years, teachers, parents, civil society organizations, volunteers, legislators, local government units, and communities have come together to confront the learning crisis and support every Filipino child.”
“This step forward demonstrates what we can achieve when the nation works together with urgency, purpose, and resolve,” it added. —With a report from Sheridan Delfino

articles.title: Remullas flying to France to seek help in finding Co
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla will also fly to France to follow up with the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) the Philippine government’s request for a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla will also fly to France to follow up with the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) the Philippine government’s request for a red notice against resigned lawmaker and fugitive Zaldy Co.

Remulla disclosed this at a press briefing on Tuesday, after his brother, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, said on Monday that he would travel to France to work with authorities there to find Co, who is believed to be seeking asylum in that country.

“We will again file a request for a red notice against Zaldy Co. Coincidentally, I am going to Lyon, France, to follow up [Co’s] red notice at the Interpol,” said the chief of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG).
Locate and arrest
An Interpol red notice is a request for law enforcement agencies worldwide to “locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, surrender, or similar legal action.”
“I will work with the Interpol. He (Ombudsman Remulla) will work with the diplomatic efforts [to get] Zaldy Co,” said the younger Remulla.
The Interpol’s headquarters are in Lyon, the city east of France that is widely acknowledged as the country’s culinary capital.
Co, who was charged in November last year in connection with a flood control project in Occidental Mindoro, was again the subject of an arrest warrant issued on Monday by the Sandiganbayan.

Apart from the resigned Ako Bicol party list lawmaker, the antigraft court also ordered the arrest of former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez for plunder. The pair is accused of receiving around P7.44 billion in kickbacks from government projects between 2022 and 2025.

The amount, according to the information filed by the Office of the Ombudsman before the Sandiganbayan, allegedly came from contractors, persons and entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and/or other government projects that were funded under the General Appropriations Act for fiscal years 2022 to 2025.
Romualdez, who is confined at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City for a “cardiovascular event,” has asked the court to allow him to remain at the hospital after his arrest.
In their motion for continued hospital confinement, his lawyers cited his “documented cardiac history,” diabetes and primary hypothyroidism, among other ailments. /cb

articles.title: Prosecutors opt to drop 15 witnesses, want to grill VP instead
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — House prosecutors on Tuesday dropped their remaining 15 witnesses on the alleged misuse of P612.5 million in confidential funds and instead, manifested their intention to call…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — House prosecutors on Tuesday dropped their remaining 15 witnesses on the alleged misuse of P612.5 million in confidential funds and instead, manifested their intention to call Vice President Sara Duterte to testify in her own impeachment trial, drawing an immediate objection from the defense.

Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said the prosecution had originally listed 27 witnesses for Article 1, which concerns the alleged misuse and misappropriation of confidential funds under the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd).
So far, 10 had been presented, while the parties had stipulated on the testimonies of two others. Three of the 15 remaining witnesses were scheduled to testify on Tuesday, Day 23 of the trial.
“In lieu of presenting 15 other witnesses, we will be presenting the Vice President herself as regards use, misuse, misappropriation of confidential funds,” Kapunan told the court.
She said the evidence already presented pointed to Duterte as the person accountable for the alleged irregularities.
VP ‘queen’ of confidential funds

“In the game chess, we have what we call pawns. There are bishops, there’s a castle, there are horses. And, the most important piece, more important than the king, and I speak this because not of my gender, but the queen is more important than the king, because the queen can move in many directions and we have seen that,” Kapunan said, using a chessboard analogy.

“We have seen that in the evidence presented, the pawns… the witnesses presented here. From the Landbank, we have been able to show that withdrawal, that there were confidential funds and these were withdrawn from two witnesses,” she added.
“All of these pawns and castles and horses and bishops point to only one person and that accountable person is the Vice President,” Kapunan declared.
But the prosecution did not seek a subpoena for Duterte yet, saying they intended to call her after presenting evidence on all four articles of impeachment.
Kapunan said Duterte’s testimony would be material to all four allegations—grave threats, misuse and misappropriation of confidential funds, unexplained wealth and bribery.
“Not at this time, your Honor,” Kapunan said when asked about a subpoena. “The testimony of the Vice President will be material to all four articles.”

The prosecution has completed its presentation on Article 4, which accuses Duterte of culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust over alleged threats against President Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and former Speaker Martin Romualdez.
The articles on unexplained wealth and bribery remain to be presented.
Defense objection
The defense immediately objected to the prospect of Duterte being compelled to testify.
Lead defense counsel Sheila Sison said there was an “innate problem” with having Duterte testify in her own trial, citing the constitutional protection against testimonial compulsion.
Sison invoked Article III, Section 17 of the 1987 Constitution, which provides that no person shall be compelled to be a witness against himself or herself.
“This is a fundamental right,” she said, stressing that the protection emanates from the Constitution.Sison also said Duterte was already participating in the proceedings through her lawyers.
“It is clear that the respondent is here through her counsel. If the respondent is not interested in this trial, she would not have even sent her lawyers to defend her in this case,” she pointed out.
The defense reserved the right to file a formal comment if the prosecution later seeks a subpoena.
House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro defended the move, saying it was consistent with the Constitution’s principles of transparency and accountability.
“It is important that the impeachment court, including the viewing public, witness how the respondent Vice President answer all these allegations,” Luistro said.
“The Filipino people have the right to hear the answer of the respondent Vice President to all these four allegations,” she added.
Court keeps Article 1 open
Presiding officer Francis Escudero directed both sides not to formally rest on Article 1 pending the court’s decision on whether to call witnesses on its own initiative.

Several senator-judges have sought testimony from former Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group commander Col. Raymund Dante Lachica and his DepEd counterpart, Col. Dennis Nolasco, particularly on who authorized and executed liquidation documents involving the confidential funds.

Escudero reminded the parties that the impeachment court may summon witnesses on its own initiative. Both sides would then be allowed to cross-examine them and present rebuttal and surrebuttal evidence.
Lachica was identified as the recipient of P500 million in OVP confidential funds from former special disbursing officer Gina Acosta, who testified that Duterte ordered the transfer.

Nolasco was also implicated in the handling of DepEd’s P112.5-million confidential funds. Duterte’s counsel and former Education Undersecretary Michael Poa previously testified that former DepEd special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda released confidential funds to Nolasco upon Duterte’s orders.
New trial calendar
The Senate has adopted a revised schedule for the impeachment trial and budget proceedings for September and October.

The September calendar is:• Sept. 7-9: Impeachment in the morning; budget hearings and legislative sessions in the afternoon.• Sept. 10-11: Budget hearings whole day.• Sept. 14-16: Impeachment in the morning; budget hearings and legislative sessions in the afternoon.• Sept. 17-18: Budget hearings whole day.• Sept. 21-23: Impeachment in the morning; budget hearings and legislative sessions in the afternoon.• Sept. 24-25: Budget hearings whole day.• Sept. 30: Session suspended.
In October, impeachment proceedings will take the whole day on Oct. 1-2, Oct. 5-9, and Oct. 12-15. Budget hearings are scheduled for Oct. 16 and Oct. 19-23, when necessary. /cb

articles.title: Impeach court revisiting ‘2/3’ conviction rule
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court will revisit the voting threshold required to convict Vice President Sara Duterte, with legal experts set to weigh in on the matter on Sept. 16…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court will revisit the voting threshold required to convict Vice President Sara Duterte, with legal experts set to weigh in on the matter on Sept. 16 before the prosecution and defense present their arguments on Sept. 23.

The court’s presiding officer, Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero, ruled to have it taken up after Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo on Tuesday formally asked the body to reconsider Escudero’s July 6 pronouncement that a vote by two-thirds of all 24 senators—or 16 votes—is needed for a conviction.
Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution provides that an impeached official cannot be convicted “without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.”

The dispute centers on whether “all members” should mean all 24 senators regardless of their ability to participate, or only those legally able to take part in the impeachment proceedings and final vote.

Four senators are currently unable to attend the trial: Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is in hiding because he faces an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court; Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta, who are detained on the nonbailable charge of plunder before the Sandiganbayan; and Loren Legarda, who is abroad on an extended medical leave.
Escudero said the court would not immediately resolve Tulfo’s appeal through the usual ayes-and-nays voting because of the “sensitive and serious nature” of the issue.

Instead, the court will hear from amici curiae, or “friends of the court,” on Sept. 16. The prosecution and Duterte’s defense will each be given 15 minutes to present their positions during oral arguments on Sept. 23, after which the Senate will vote on the threshold question.

Escudero said the legal experts could provide independent expertise and perspectives on the constitutional issue. Their names have yet to be announced as the court is still confirming their availability.
Legal experts split
Senator-judge Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan said the amici could include eminent legal experts, retired chief justices or Supreme Court justices, and constitutional law specialists.
The question has already drawn differing views from retired Supreme Court justices and a former president of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP).

Former Supreme Court Associate Justice Adolfo Azcuna, in an ANC interview on June 19, said he believed the 16-vote requirement should remain because the Constitution refers to the membership of the Senate, not merely those physically present.
“My view is that the voting threshold is based on the number of members of the Senate whether or not those members are present or able to actively participate,” Azcuna said.

“As long as they remain members of the Senate they should be counted in computing the two-thirds,” he added, maintaining that the threshold remained 16 because the four senators unable to participate were still members of the chamber.

Azcuna, however, raised a possible exception involving Dela Rosa, saying that if the senator is legally considered a fugitive, his status could potentially amount to a constructive resignation because he had placed himself outside the legal system.
Retired Supreme Court Senior Associate Justice Antonio Carpio took a different position.
In a June 21 post on his website, Carpio argued that the two-thirds computation should be based on senators who are legally qualified to participate in the proceedings.
“If you cannot hold office, you cannot vote,” Carpio said.
Carpio nevertheless noted that Dela Rosa remained a qualified senator because he had neither been suspended nor removed from office.

Former IBP president Domingo Cayosa, meanwhile, said in an interview with the Inquirer on July 11 that the 16-vote threshold could be lowered to reflect the senators actually able to participate in the impeachment trial.
Cayosa described this as a “fair and practical” reading of the Constitution, saying it was consistent with the Charter’s spirit, which he characterized as “not restrictive.”
The operative phrase, he said, was “two-thirds” of all members of the Senate.

Estrada, Dela Rosa and Marcoleta “are all alive and are not yet unseated by any of the constitutionally allowed modes of removal, so they are still senators,” Cayosa said. “Except when they transform themselves into an impeachment court, they all become judges.”
That distinction, he said, creates a constitutional nuance: “because how can you be a judge when you were not there, [and] you did not observe and participate.”
But Cayosa acknowledged that a “simple and strictly literal” reading of the Constitution, particularly from the defense’s perspective, would keep the threshold at 16.
Tulfo seeks clarification
Tulfo raised the issue on Tuesday, asking whether senators who are unable to attend the trial should nevertheless be allowed to vote.
“When we refer to all members, who exactly are we counting?” Tulfo asked.
He questioned whether the absent senators’ votes would be accepted despite their nonparticipation, or whether their absence would effectively count as a vote against conviction.
Tulfo warned that retaining a fixed 24-member voting base could result in an “acquittal by default” if enough senators were unable to cast votes.
He cited Avelino v. Cuenco, which he said considers members within the Senate’s coercive jurisdiction in determining the voting base and quorum.
Senator-judge Pia Cayetano disputed the argument, saying it was inaccurate to suggest that the Senate had adopted the Supreme Court ruling as its governing rule.

Escudero clarified that Tulfo’s appeal seeks a determination of what constitutes “all members” under the Constitution. He also pointed out that changing the voting base would affect not only the two-thirds requirement for conviction but also the one-third threshold for acquittal.

Tulfo said the matter should be resolved quickly because the trial calendar has been expedited, with the prosecution dropping several witnesses and Duterte’s defense indicating it might not present its own case.
“These developments … could bring the court to the final question sooner than expected,” Tulfo said.
He stressed that he was not seeking to make conviction easier, but to settle how the constitutional requirement should operate under the Senate’s present circumstances.
“What we should ask ourselves this time … should the constitutional design of making impeachment difficult, override equally important constitutional demand for accountability?” he said.
Escudero said the court would take the matter under advisement, hear the amici and the parties, and then decide. —With a report from Inquirer Research

articles.title: Buckingham reminder: Harry, Meghan still nonworking royals
articles.summary: LONDON — Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, were surprised by the way Buckingham Palace released a letter that made clear they remain nonworking members of the royal family even though they have…

blocks.text: LONDON — Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, were surprised by the way Buckingham Palace released a letter that made clear they remain nonworking members of the royal family even though they have returned to the United Kingdom.

The letter, sent on behalf of King Charles III to senior government and military officials, caught the couple off guard when it was released to the media on Monday in part because they were given little time to review or comment on its contents, a person familiar with the discussions said.
Little time to respond

The couple’s representatives received a copy of the letter just one hour and 12 minutes before it was released to news outlets, the person said. That left them with little time to respond because they were unable to reach Harry, who was in a meeting, until just two minutes before the letter was released, the person added.

The letter said Harry and Meghan would continue to refrain from using the formal royal titles, such as his royal highness and her royal highness, as they have done since stepping back from official royal duties in 2020. Any charity work the couple undertakes will be carried out in a private capacity, and operational security decisions are matters for the relevant police agencies, the letter said.
Avoid doubt, confusion
“To help avoid doubt or confusion, The King has directed that (this) information be shared,” the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior official in the royal household, said in the letter.
Harry and Meghan stepped back from royal duties in 2020 when they moved to North America to make their own living through lucrative deals with Netflix and Spotify.

At the time, Queen Elizabeth II made clear that the couple could not be part-time royals and they had to give up their royal positions if they wanted to pursue such commercial arrangements. Charles reiterated that position after he became king in 2022. /cb

articles.title: MMDA chief Torre goes on monthlong leave after Edsa Busway controversy
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Nicolas Torre III went on a monthlong leave effective Tuesday, after he admitted to committing several…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Nicolas Torre III went on a monthlong leave effective Tuesday, after he admitted to committing several violations when he used the Edsa Busway lane reserved for passenger buses, on-duty emergency vehicles, and cars being used by the country’s top five government officials.

Torre earlier apologized and paid a fine for using the exclusive bus lane. He also admitted to fitting his armored sport utility vehicle with a license plate that had been issued to another car, an MMDA logo and a blinker to make it look like an official MMDA vehicle.
MMDA Chair Don Artes said that Torre, who was appointed by President Marcos to the agency in December last year, even considered retiring from public service following public backlash.

“‘Don’t do anything rash,’ I told him. Just contemplate, because, first of all, as I have said, General Torre has been a big help to me, especially with the day-to-day operations of the MMDA,” Artes added.
During his short-lived stint as Philippine National Police chief in 2025, Torre gained public admiration for his no-nonsense leadership style and reputation as an advocate for good governance.
Artes said he did not issue a suspension order against Torre because he lacks “disciplinary authority” over him, citing his presidential appointment.

He also denied giving Torre any “special treatment,” stressing that the MMDA official has already been fined while his vehicle would not be released until all the unauthorized markings and equipment have been removed.

“I can categorically say that I still trust him and in my opinion, he is still an asset to the agency despite what happened. Because, first of all, our job does not just revolve around traffic,” said Artes.

“Traffic is just one out of [our] seven [mandates]. So, this issue might have an impact in so far as traffic matters are concerned, especially enforcement of traffic laws. But as to all other mandates, I don’t think it will affect those,” he added. /cb

articles.title: Prosecution to ICC: Admit witness’ testimony on Duterte ‘DDS’ model
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution in the International Criminal Court (ICC) has asked a trial chamber to admit as evidence the previously recorded testimony of a witness who has proof of the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution in the International Criminal Court (ICC) has asked a trial chamber to admit as evidence the previously recorded testimony of a witness who has proof of the “Davao Death Squad” (DDS) model allegedly masterminded by former President Rodrigo Duterte.

In a redacted version of the Aug. 31 request sent to the Trial Chamber III, the prosecution sought the submission of the testimony of the witness referred to as “P-1100,” calling it “relevant, reliable and probative” to Duterte’s antinarcotics policy that ordered the killing of suspected criminals, including drug users and traders.

Duterte, who is being held at the Scheveningen prison complex in The Hague, the Netherlands, is charged with three counts of murder in his crimes against humanity case for being criminally responsible for the drug war killings that happened while he was Davao City mayor and later on, as President.

“It primarily relates to [redacted]. As such, his evidence is particularly relevant to the policy to ‘neutralise’ through violent crimes, including murder, alleged criminals in the Philippines. It also provides evidence of the (DDS) modus operandi, as well as the accused’s (Duterte’s) individual criminal responsibility, including in relation to his knowledge and intent,” read part of the eight-page filing.

The prosecution said that allowing the testimony to be introduced as evidence would also give the defense and legal representatives of victims opportunities to cross-examine P-1100 during the trial, which begins on Nov. 30.

They cited Rule 68(3) in the ICC Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which allows the chamber to introduce previously recorded testimony during trial without any objection and as long as all parties to the case are given time to examine the witness during the proceedings.

Admitting the documented testimony as evidence would also significantly cut the duration of direct examination, expedite court proceedings and save court time by at least five hours, the prosecution said.

The testimony of P-1100, who is referred to as a “he” in the documents, is considered “corroborative and cumulative” of the evidence provided by at least four witnesses expected to testify in court. They were identified only as “P-0001,” “P-0026,” “P1022” and “P-1390.”

“P-1100’s prior recorded testimony is internally consistent and accompanied by supporting documents in relation to certain aspects. It is also cumulative in nature and corroborative of other evidence,” the prosecution said. /cb

articles.title: Pacquiao joins Marcos Cabinet as antipoverty czar
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Barely a year after he returned to the boxing ring, former Sen. Manny Pacquiao will have to shift his focus back to public service with his appointment as the government’s…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Barely a year after he returned to the boxing ring, former Sen. Manny Pacquiao will have to shift his focus back to public service with his appointment as the government’s antipoverty czar.

During a ceremony on Tuesday at Malacañang, President Marcos swore in the 47-year-old Pacquiao, the only eight-division world champion in boxing history, as lead convener of the National Anti-Poverty Commission (NAPC), with a rank of Cabinet secretary.
He replaced Lope Santos III, who had served as NAPC lead convener since 2023. Malacañang did not say why it replaced Santos, who nevertheless congratulated his successor.

Established through Republic Act No. 8425, the NAPC coordinates poverty reduction programs by national and local governments and ensures that marginalized sectors participate in government decision-making processes.

It is chaired by Marcos, while Pacquiao, as lead convener, shall serve as head of the NAPC Secretariat to direct daily operations, interagency convergence and institutional engagement with the country’s 14 basic sectors.

Pacquiao thanked Marcos for allowing him to help more Filipinos, saying his new government role was rooted in his experience. “I came from poverty … That is why my heart is truly with the poor,” he said.
Pacquiao’s post is different from Secretary Larry Gadon’s, the presidential adviser for poverty alleviation. —Dexter Cabalza

articles.title: Baguio group asks council to block horror fest
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — A Christian group has asked the city council to block a planned horror convention in October, saying it could undermine the city’s values and promote imagery of death,…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — A Christian group has asked the city council to block a planned horror convention in October, saying it could undermine the city’s values and promote imagery of death, violence and the occult.
Marketing professional Eric Pangilinan, who launched an online petition opposing the event, appeared before the council on Monday with members of the Endtimes Harvest Christian Ministry.

They objected to the Baguio Horror Festival, a privately organized Halloween event scheduled for Oct. 24 to Oct. 25 along Session Road, saying organizers intend to make Baguio the “horror capital of the Philippines.”
“Death and destruction. Darkness. Zombies. They want to make the city the melting pot of horror. We want to keep Baguio the character city that it is,” Pangilinan told the council.
The petition cited Baguio’s 2023 ordinance promoting “positive values” and urged the city to withhold permits, personnel and the use of city-owned venues and streets for the festival.

The group also cited recent cases of school violence, including a Department of Education tally of 135 bullying incidents in Baguio during school year 2024-2025, as part of its argument against staging horror-themed events.
The petitioners acknowledged that they were not claiming horror festivals caused violence, but said recent incidents had heightened concerns among parents and communities.
They proposed replacing horror-themed events with a harvest festival, cultural parade or other activities aligned with Baguio’s “Character City” campaign.
Baguio has long been associated with ghost stories, with places such as the former Diplomat Hotel and Laperal White House often linked to alleged hauntings.

Young residents have also held Halloween activities, including the “Karkarna” zombie walk, which began in 2011 and has drawn cosplayers and students. The event, however, was not held in 2024 and 2025.

While Pangilinan said the appeal was not intended to ban or criminalize Halloween activities, the group’s petition also raised religious objections to events featuring zombie, occult and death imagery.
The petition cited Christian scripture and literature associated with Halloween and Satanism, saying its opposition was rooted partly in concerns over the religious implications of such imagery. /cb

articles.title: ‘Habagat,’ 4 cyclones leave P4.38-B agri damage
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The combined effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon or “habagat,” and Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok have damaged P4.38 billion worth of agricultural…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The combined effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon or “habagat,” and Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok have damaged P4.38 billion worth of agricultural produce nationwide.

In its final bulletin posted on Tuesday, the Department of Agriculture (DA) said the weather disturbances affected the livelihood of 99,663 farmers and fisherfolk in Cordillera, Ilocos, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, Quezon), Mimaropa (Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, Palawan), Bicol and Western Visayas regions.

Also damaged were 102,791 metric tons of farm produce, reaching 81,511 hectares, with rice accounting for 46.69 percent of the overall damage estimated at P2.05 billion. High-value crops came second at 31.44 percent or P1.38 billion of the total, followed by fisheries at 14.79 percent or P647.79 million.

Other affected commodities included corn, cassava, livestock and poultry, and agri-fisheries infrastructure, machinery and equipment. The DA said it is crafting a comprehensive rehabilitation and recovery plan for agriculture, particularly in affected areas. —Jordeene B. Lagare

articles.title: Why India’s economic data has sparked a furore
articles.summary:
India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have eroded

There isn’t much that we Indians agree…

blocks.text: There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.

Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.

The assertion, made on a television channel, immediately went viral. A flurry of op-eds and hot takes have been published since. Supporters of the government, predictably, rejected the claims. Those who have questions agree on a more fundamental problem: a lack of transparency and statistical credibility in India’s economic data. So why is there no consensus?

Over the past decade, critics say, the government has systematically hollowed out the integrity of its own data infrastructure, weaponising economic data for political gain and creating a trust deficit. Methodologies have been changed, crucial surveys have faced long delays and there have been attempts to suppress inconvenient findings.

In November, the International Monetary Fund rated India’s national accounts data a ‘C’ on a four-point scale, the second-lowest grade. In its report, the IMF said some of the methodologies are outdated, including relying on an old base year, unexplained discrepancies between GDP calculated from the production and expenditure side, as well as a lack of seasonal data.

blocks.caption: Critics say the government has hollowed out the integrity of its own data infrastructure. Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty Images

blocks.text: India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous. There might have been disagreements on the quality of estimates but their independence was widely accepted. That trust appears to have eroded in recent years.

“There seems to be a systematic effort by the government to hide the truth,” said R Nagaraj, an economist who taught at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research, adding that some of the other contested datasets include employment numbers, poverty numbers, health data and consumption data. “Over the last 10 years, the government has changed the methodology for many of these, raising questions. They have apparently also removed critical officials who headed some surveys. All of this adds to the scepticism.”

In one of the most prominent examples, from 2019, a Business Standard journalist revealed that the government had not published an official report showing unemployment at a 45-year high of 6.1%. Two expert members of the National Statistical Commission resigned in protest. The government initially denied it, calling it a draft. The figures were only released months later.

Then there is the census, which for the first time since independence, was delayed in 2021. Economists say relying on outdated demographic data means, among other things, inequitable allocation of welfare entitlements. (The first phase of the latest census finally began in April 2026.)

Nagaraj has witnessed some of this first-hand. He served on a subcommittee in 2014 whose report forms a part of the GDP. “The [numbers] we had discussed in the committee and what came out in the final report were different. So, I had to raise a red flag,” he said. The difference was notable: one figure in the published report had been inflated by 108%.

But government economists reject the ongoing criticism of the GDP numbers. Shamika Ravi, a member of the Economic Advisory Council to the prime minister, described it as a “noisy and very ill-informed debate” arguing that political leanings, not data, are behind the criticism.

The IMF rating was expected, she said. “The IMF rating of ‘C’ is the same rating that China has for its statistics. Several large developing or just developed economies have data issues.” Revisions to its calculations that the government was accused of having manipulated, she added, were precisely the sorts of changes the IMF had recommended.
The sticking point, as some including India’s former chief statistician Pronab Sen have pointed out, is the trustworthiness of the underlying data used.

Complicating this debate is the reality for many Indians. This year, young people have taken to the streets in frustration. Protests, which first began over leaked examination papers, have crystallised into a broader reckoning over systemic failures in education, jobs and the promise of a better future.

blocks.caption: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke at a protest against leaked exam papers, as young people in India face soaring rates of unemployment. Photograph: Arun Sankar/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Almost 40% of graduates under 25 are unemployed, a recent report by Azim Premji University concluded. An estimated 87 million (8.7 crore) Indians between 15 and 29 are neither working, studying, nor doing skill training, a government thinktank reported last month.

That is why we should care about data quality, economists say. Incorrect data means bad policy. As economist Reetika Khera wrote in her recent book, Freebies or Rights: “Data shines the light to guide policymaking and is important for informed public debates.” As evidence, she points to gaps in basic statistics such as urbanisation and literacy numbers due to the delayed census. The consequences, she argues, are not abstract. Because the government still relies on outdated population numbers to decide who gets food subsidies, she estimates approximately 100 million (10 crore) people who should be covered are being deprived.

The controversy is making waves further ashore. In Sri Lanka, where second-quarter GDP figures are expected, the Daily FT newspaper wrote: “One hopes Sri Lankan policymakers and experts are not watching the theatrics in India with watering mouths and dreaming up smart arguments. Spare us such theatre!”
What else we’re reading about

blocks.caption: Mumbai bound … British singer Olivia Dean is headed to Lollapalooza. Photograph: Isabel Infantes/Reuters

blocks.text: Lollapalooza | British pop star Olivia Dean is to perform in India for the first time in January when she headlines Lollapalooza 2027 in Mumbai. Limp Bizkit is another headline act at the two-day event. Indian artists on the lineup include Ricky Kej (performing with Stewart Copeland) and Aditya Gadhvi.

The price of gold | Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked Indians once again to refrain from buying gold and travelling abroad. He had first made an appeal to self-reliance in May, in part to conserve India’s declining foreign exchange reserves amid a rise in import prices and global energy shocks.

Census 2027 | The new and expanded questionnaire for the 2027 census is raising concerns, reports Scroll’s Anant Gupta. The questionnaire asks respondents for details about their identity documents, as well as their parents’ religion and place of birth. Several of these questions were part of the controversial National Population Register that has remained in abeyance since 2020 and was controversial due to fears that the data might be used to target minorities through a citizenship registry.
after newsletter promotion
Guest shelf
A recommendation from someone with great taste

blocks.caption: Bean-to-bar movement … artisanal chocolate is having a moment. Photograph: Manam

blocks.text: Singer Prateek Kuhad (@prateekkuhad), whose latest album, Full Moon Chamber, was released in July, shares an indulgent treat: “I’m a big fan of artisanal Indian chocolate makers. I really like Manam, Carra and Naviluna, and there are many others. Although India has been growing cacao [commercially] since the 1960s, its craft bean-to-bar movement is more recent. Even a plain chocolate bar from one of these makers can be remarkably complex and delicious. More people outside India should know about it and try it.”
Count it
A number worth knowing

blocks.caption: A controversial revision … one-third of the electorate in Delhi have been deleted from voter lists. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: One-third of the electorate in Delhi, about 4.76 million voters, have been deleted from the draft voting list as the Election Commission carries out a contentious revision of its rolls across states. So far, about 130 million names have been dropped from draft rolls in 30 states and union territories, the Indian Express reported.
Vibe check

blocks.caption: First of many mashups … Ismail Langa Group pose with a larger-than-life image of Shakira. Photograph: Ismail Langa

blocks.text: Earlier this year, Shakira’s concerts in India was postponed. But Rajasthani folk musicians the Ismail Langa Group (@ismaillanga_official) decided the music had to go on, in their own way. Their mashup of the Colombian star’s Hips Don’t Lie with the traditional folk song called Moruda has got everyone grooving (42m views and counting).

It took two months to pull off, says creative director Jagirdar RV. Most artists in the group, aged between 23 and 60, don’t speak or read English and learned the lyrics by rote. The song choice was simple, he said, because it “has a very nice vibe which matched our vibe”.

It’s been a breakout year for the group, which had a semi-final run on India’s Got Talent and are becoming known for taking folk songs to gen Z audiences on Instagram. They are working on their next English mashup – just not spilling which song, yet.
